Why China’s manufacturing machine endures The stubborn persistence of Chinese inputs in overseas supply chains reflects the country’s unrivalled strength across a wide range of industries. The Morgan Stanley report found that China’s share of value-added content in global imports increased in 10 of 13 manufacturing sectors over the past decade, with gains in both lower-value-added industries such as textiles, leather and footwear and more technologically advanced sectors. In 2024, for instance, China accounted for 33 per cent of the value-added content in global imports of electrical and optical equipment, 24 per cent in machinery and equipment and 10 per cent in transport equipment. “These patterns are consistent with China retaining higher-value production processes even as final assembly moves elsewhere, while China continues to supply the equipment and inputs needed by new manufacturing hubs,” the analysts said. Meanwhile, China’s exports surged 36.3 per cent year on year to US$447.18 billion last month, customs data showed on Wednesday. The momentum – driven by strong global tech demand and a pre-holiday shipping rush ahead of the “golden week” break – logged a monthly high for its trade surplus in 2026 and put the country on course for another record gap this year. A separate report from Goldman Sachs last week examined China’s rising proportion of global exports. According to the bank’s analysis, that share increased from 4 per cent in 2000 to 15 per cent in 2025, outpacing the peaks previously reached by Germany in the 1970s and Japan in the 1980s. “Our benchmarking exercise implies that robust real export growth [in China] can continue over the next few years,” the bank’s analysts said. “The runway is therefore clear for now – but eventually will depend on stronger economic growth in importing economies.” The Morgan Stanley report also highlighted emerging technologies as a potential source of further growth. “China is increasingly playing a critical role in global supply chains, not just in low-cost component supplies but also in high-end capital goods as well,” the analysts wrote. “Our China team also believes China’s advantage in global manufacturing will be strengthened as it enters a new phase of industrial development in the form of ‘Industry 5.0’”, they added, referring to manufacturing enabled by artificial intelligence and robotics. An earlier report by Morgan Stanley released in May argued humanoids and other robotics technologies could help China consolidate its dominance over global manufacturing, building on its decade-long expansion in electric vehicle manufacturing. The bank’s analysts projected that China’s share of global exports would reach 16.5 per cent by 2030, up from about 15 per cent at the time of the report. For countries pushing to become alternative manufacturing hubs, the findings suggest they would also need to develop the suppliers, expertise and networks that China has spent decades building. “Diversification is achievable, but decoupling will be challenging,” the analysts argued.

title: Meet Steve Buscemi’s new wife, Karen Ho, who attended the Wild Horse Nine screening in London
description: The Reservoir Dogs actor was married to Jo Andres until she died in 2019 and has since relocated from Brooklyn to Manhattan with his new love.
content: After the tragic passing of his wife, Jo Andres, in 2019, Steve Buscemi seems to have found happiness again with his new wife, Karen Ho, whom he married in 2025. On October 9, the Wednesday actor and Ho arrived hand in hand at the screening of his film Wild Horse Nine at the Royal Festival Hall in London during the BFI London Film Festival. Buscemi was previously married to Andres, an artist and filmmaker, for over three decades until she passed away after battling cancer. She was 64 years old. Buscemi and Andres share a son, Lucian, who was born in 1990. Fortunately for Buscemi, he found love again with Karen Ho. Here’s everything you need to know about Steve Buscemi’s second wife. What does Karen Ho do? Unlike her famous husband, Ho has built a life outside the limelight. There is little information available on her and, according to The New York Times, she does not work in the entertainment industry. Nevertheless, Ho has shown her support for her husband by attending multiple red carpet events with him. She lives in Manhattan with Buscemi Buscemi and Ho quietly wed in 2025. There is little information on how they met or how long they were dating before tying the knot, and the actor has continued to divulge little about his second marriage to the public. In a 2025 interview with The New York Times, he mentioned that he and Ho had “totally different” tastes in films. He also revealed that he had moved to Manhattan with Ho, where they had found a new place together. What has Steve Buscemi said about his late wife? Although the 68-year-old actor is generally quite private about his personal life, he did open up about Andres’ passing in a 2020 interview with GQ. Buscemi said he had been emptying their three-story brownstone in Brooklyn, New York, adding that the house felt too big for him after her death. On a more personal level, Buscemi said: “If I should happen to go, not suddenly, I hope I could be as present as Jo was. She led the way. She was surrounded by friends and family. She really faced it. I really don’t think she was afraid of dying. I think it was just a whole series of ‘Oh, I don’t get to do this any more.’”

title: Visa’s China approval a ‘direct outcome’ of Xi-Trump summit, Beijing says
description: Visa CEO among White House guests at state dinner honouring Chinese leader last month and also attended Trump’s visit to Beijing in May.
content: China said on Thursday that the recent government approval allowing American bank card payment giant Visa to operate in the country was the “direct outcome” of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the United States last month. “The Visa card was granted permission to establish a banking card clearing institution,” said Qiu Wenxing, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Chinese embassy in Washington. “It is a direct outcome of the presidential summit.” Visa received administrative approval on Tuesday from the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) to make preparations for a locally registered bank card clearing organisation, a move the central bank described as a major step in opening up the country’s financial sector. The US card payment company will have one year to complete its advance arrangements, after which it may apply to begin operations, the central bank said in an online statement. Visa has established a foreign-invested company, Visa Information Technology (Beijing), in China to operate there. American Express began domestic bank card clearing operations through a Chinese joint venture in 2020, while Mastercard’s joint venture received approval in 2023. Unlike its competitors, Visa plans to operate through a wholly foreign-owned enterprise. Visa initially applied for the PBOC approval in July 2017. A central bank official told Chinese media in 2019 that the company withdrew its application in January 2018, resubmitted revised materials three months later and was awaiting a decision. Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said in a statement on Tuesday that the approval marked “a significant step forward in Visa’s long-standing commitment to China”. “We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies,” he said. “For more than 40 years, Visa has been an active contributor to China’s dynamic payments landscape. “We look forward to taking the necessary steps in the process, pursuant to the PBOC’s regulations, to begin operating domestically in China.” McInerney was among the high-profile guests at last month’s White House state dinner in honour of the Chinese leader and also joined the delegation of CEOs who accompanied US President Donald Trump on his state visit to Beijing in May. In its press statement, Visa said that “China is one of the world’s most advanced and dynamic digital payments markets”, supported by a “highly innovative ecosystem and continued commitment to further financial sector liberalisation”. “Visa looks forward to bringing its world-class innovation, security and reliability to Chinese consumers and businesses, contributing to the continued development of China’s domestic payments landscape,” it added. The Chinese embassy on Thursday said the financial services agreement was part of the 10-point consensus reached at last month’s summit, alongside other outcomes including the launch of the Board of Trade and a two-month extension of the Busan agreement. “The two sides reached a consensus on the principle of financial services,” the embassy said. It added that China welcomes financial institutions from all countries, including the US, to expand their business and establish operations in the country. “China hopes the US will also provide a fair, transparent and stable environment for Chinese financial institutions,” it noted.

title: Trump press secretary Katie Zacharia never passed bar exam, wrongly claims China has none
description: Katie Zacharia admits she failed California bar exam and questions China’s rise, saying the country does not even have ‘proper toilets’.
content: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia has acknowledged that she never passed a bar exam, days after telling reporters she had passed one “when I moved to China”. In an interview with the conservative commentator Jack Posobiec on right-wing streaming channel Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Zacharia said she sat the California bar exam after graduating from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011 but did not pass. She said the results were “somewhat inconsequential, because I knew I wouldn’t need the bar in China”, where she moved with her husband for his job. “There’s no Chinese bar,” she said. “I had enough credentials, which was my law degree.” China does have a bar exam. The National Unified Legal Professional Qualification Examination is required to practice as a lawyer on the mainland, but only Chinese citizens may sit it, under rules set by China’s Ministry of Justice. Chinese law firms can hire foreign nationals, but they cannot be licensed as lawyers in China. Zacharia told Posobiec there had been “a lot of misinformation” about the fact that she “labelled myself ‘lawyer’”, and that “absolutely across the board you can call yourself a lawyer”. She said she had consulted “many people in the field”, without naming them. She told the New York Times on Wednesday that Pepperdine’s president had advised her she could call herself a “lawyer” but not an “attorney” or “esquire”. In the same interview, asked how she balanced her personal life with her work, Zacharia gave a lengthy answer in which she said US President Donald Trump’s 2016 election victory had put the United States back on the path to greatness. “I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,’” she said. The State Bar of California, which regulates lawyers in the state, told the South China Morning Post that it had no record of Zacharia having been licensed under either her married name or her maiden name, Black. It said that, as a general matter, state law makes it unlawful for anyone who is not an active licensee, or otherwise authorised, to hold themselves out as practising or entitled to practice law in California. Trump called Zacharia an attorney when he announced her appointment last week. She had previously said she practised international transaction law “with all the appropriate credentials”, and told the Times on Wednesday that she had misheard Tuesday’s question about the bar exam over the noise of the presidential helicopter. On her LinkedIn profile, Zacharia lists herself as an associate at Zhong Lun Law Firm, one of China’s largest, from 2011 to 2013. She told Posobiec she was “offered a job at an international practice division of a Chinese law firm”. Gary Gao, a Shanghai-based partner at the firm, told the Times that Zhong Lun often hired foreigners for language assistance and that “they are not practising Chinese law at any time”. He said her role would likely have resembled a paid internship. Zacharia has also said on a podcast that she had been “the outside counsel to the IFC and the World Bank”, according to a clip first identified by the independent journalist Judd Legum. On Wednesday, Campaign for Accountability – a watchdog group that does not disclose its donors – asked the State Bar to investigate whether Zacharia had broken state law by holding herself out as a lawyer, and whether her work as general counsel of Fix California, a non-profit organisation led by former Trump administration official Richard Grenell, amounted to unauthorised practice. The group told the South China Morning Post that the State Bar had acknowledged receiving the complaint, and that it had also shared it with the DC Bar. Michelle Kuppersmith, its executive director, said the distinction between “lawyer” and “attorney” was “a distinction without a difference”. “She was not entitled to hold herself out as a lawyer,” she said. The State Bar said it could not confirm whether it had received a complaint or was investigating, as disciplinary matters are confidential. The White House did not respond to repeated requests for comment from the SCMP. Zhong Lun did not respond to a request for comment.

title: Opinion | Beyond baby bonuses: Hong Kong needs to attract couples with liveability
description: Tokyo’s struggle to hold on to young adults looking to start families should inform Hong Kong’s efforts to boost the city’s birth rate.
content: Hong Kong’s efforts to boost the number of newborns in the city should be considered in the context of talent retention relating to Hong Kong’s liveability. When the Census and Statistics Department reported in August that births in Hong Kong had fallen by an annualised 15.6 per cent to a historic low of fewer than 30,000, it injected a sharp sense of urgency into public discussions as Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu prepared to deliver his policy address. The government addressed concerns with 11 measures to raise the birth rate. They include extending the HK$20,000 (US$2,500) baby bonus for newborns, increasing tax incentives for families with more than one child, raising mortgage caps and lowering stamp duty for households raising children, and strengthening after-school care. Couples and prospective parents are likely to welcome such measures, but cash grants and subsidies only address short-term challenges. If Hong Kong is to reverse its demographic decline and win the global competition for talent, it must look beyond technical incentives and explore other ways to enhance its appeal as a liveable city. The central question facing policymakers is how to retain talented people through not just incentives but also lifestyle measures. What can Hong Kong offer these people so they feel confident about working here, starting families and making Hong Kong their home? Tokyo provides a useful case study in this effort. The Japanese capital is often viewed as a textbook example of East Asia’s demographic squeeze, but a 2025 survey of nearly 10,000 residents by the Tokyo metropolitan government revealed that the desire to form families remained strong. More than 80 per cent of married respondents identified one to three children as their ideal family size, while only 10 per cent expressed no wish to have children. The obstacle is not a lack of ambition but the reality of urban strain. High education costs, compact housing and relentless workplace pressures force couples to scale back their plans. The consequences of such pressure are reflected in Tokyo’s migration patterns. Tokyo gained more than 60,000 young adults in their 20s each year between 2019 and 2023, confirming its appeal to students and early-career talent. In that same period, though, it lost more than 34,000 residents in their 30s. Tokyo becomes a leaky bucket as people turn from building careers to starting families. Mid-career professionals exit the urban core for neighbouring prefectures such as Saitama, Chiba and Kanagawa, or they relocate to regional hubs such as Osaka and Fukuoka in search of family-friendly liveability. This mobility shift carries serious economic consequences. Professionals in their 30s represent some of a city’s most productive workforce, highest earners and primary tax base. When they leave, they take their skills, consumer spending and the next generation of human capital with them. Hong Kong faces a similar challenge. It retains considerable strengths, including global and regional connectivity, a dynamic economy, efficient transport and the potential for cross-border hi-tech development in the Northern Metropolis. However, as cross-border connectivity improves, Greater Bay Area cities might become a more practical living option for Hong Kong families. Unlike Japanese couples, women in Hong Kong have little incentive to have a second child, contributing to a steady decline in the city’s birth count. In a 2024 survey of one-child households, only 31 per cent of respondents had a clear intention to have a second child. Those who were unsure or did not wish to have another child cited reasons such as insufficient daytime childcare support for working parents and an inflexible work culture. This poses a real question for Hong Kong’s long-term population planning. Attracting global talent through recruitment schemes is only a short-term achievement if those same professionals leave the moment they become parents. Japan’s national government recognises that practical supports alone fall short. Under its broader population strategy, amendments to the Child Care and Family Care Leave Act have introduced reforms mandating statutory flexible-working options and stronger childcare-leave protections for working parents. Tokyo has taken extra steps in reinforcing these national mandates with its own local incentives and public campaigns, striving to make the capital a more attractive, liveable home for talented people, married couples and growing families. Tokyo’s experience offers Hong Kong a timely lesson. Genuine population policy must extend beyond financial incentives to overhaul the everyday experience of city life, from workplace culture to lifestyle and community support. To secure its future, Hong Kong must renew its urban image around genuine liveability. Reimagining population planning through a citywide lifestyle lens does more than boost birth rates; it creates a sustainable ecosystem that ensures seamless succession not just within our corporate boardrooms but across our families and communities. That is how “Asia’s world city” can truly renew itself as a place where local and global talent alike feel confident putting down roots for generations to come.

title: Yemen’s Houthis attack presidential palace in Aden with missiles
description: Prime minister survives deadly strike as Riyadh points the finger at Tehran over widening war.
content: The Houthis launched a deadly missile attack Thursday on the presidential palace in the Yemeni government’s interim capital of Aden, as Saudi Arabia blamed Iran for the recent dramatic escalation in the long-running war. The attack hit command centres located inside the Al-Maashiq presidential compound used by government forces and the Saudi-led military coalition that supports them, a Yemeni minister said on condition of anonymity. Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government it backs have come under sustained Houthi attack of late, shifting the focus of the wider Middle East war that erupted with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. The Iran-backed Houthis have seized swathes of territory along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in recent weeks, and a government counteroffensive with Saudi air support has so far failed to reverse the gains. Yemeni health minister Qasim Buhaibeh said Thursday’s attack left five people dead and 16 injured “among those working to guard the site and civilian employees”. An Agence France-Presse journalist saw smoke rising and residents of the southern city reported hearing explosions during the attack, the first on the complex since Yemen’s civil war flared back to life in July. Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the “cowardly” act on X, calling it a “continuation of its criminal pattern of striking civilian sites and civilians”. A government minister said on condition of anonymity that Zindani had been present at the time, but “was not harmed in any way”. The minister said the Houthis hit a command centre for Yemeni government forces with three missiles, and another for Saudi-led coalition forces at the complex with two missiles, adding that there were Yemeni and Saudi casualties, without providing a specific toll. Media affiliated with the Houthis said they had targeted “the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them”. Yemen’s civil war – in which Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting the government since 2015 – reignited after the collapse of a years-long truce, with the Houthis going on to launch their lightning offensive in September. Riyadh on Thursday accused Iran of encouraging the escalation, saying it continued to arm and train the group. Saudi Arabia’s deputy minister for public diplomacy at the foreign ministry said Riyadh was still in touch with Iran, but that Tehran did not appear ready to make concessions. “We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran,” said Dr Rayed Krimly. The Saudi-led coalition said drones fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southern region and the city of Khamis Mushait were intercepted. Yemeni government forces said the Houthis had also fired “several ballistic missiles” at the central city of Marib, which sits in a strategic oil-rich region. In 2023, regional rivals Iran and Saudi Arabia reached a deal mediated by China to thaw a long-standing freeze in ties, but the latest violence might threaten to upend the entente. The Saudi ministry official went on to accuse the Houthis of refusing to meet as fighting ramped up between the two sides. “At the beginning of this escalation, we asked them to meet in Muscat, Oman and they refused,” he added. The ministry later said that the exchange took place in July. Saudi Arabia suffered its deadliest attack in more than a decade on Saturday when a strike on Riyadh’s international airport killed 13 people and wounded around 300 others. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said the group had attacked Riyadh’s airport 20 times this month. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said “the Houthis must immediately cease all terrorist operations targeting civilians and civilian facilities, including airports, ports, oil facilities, and infrastructure”. He added the group had “worked to obtain advanced technologies with the help of regional actors”, saying they now had “ballistic missiles, attack and suicide drones, and fast explosive-laden boats”. The attacks on Saudi Arabia have tested the country’s infrastructure and resilience, the energy minister acknowledged earlier this week. Riyadh usually hosts a packed calendar of events this time of year, including its flagship investment conference drawing foreign leaders and business titans. In Yemen, the conflict has caused what the United Nations calls one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, leaving most of the nation’s population dependent on aid.

title: China bought half of Brazil’s oil exports as Iran war shut Hormuz, driving sales to record
description: Crude makes up a quarter of Brazilian shipments to Chinese buyers, but growth has slowed since Gulf tankers started sailing again.
content: Trade between Brazil and China reached a record US$143 billion in the first nine months of the year, driven by Brazilian oil sales that surged after the war on Iran disrupted Gulf supply, according to a report by the Brazil-China Business Council. Brazilian exports to China rose 12 per cent to US$84.7 billion between January and September, while imports from China grew 9.9 per cent to US$58.6 billion, the council said in its quarterly analysis of government data. The resulting US$26.1 billion surplus equalled 42 per cent of Brazil’s trade surplus with the world. Crude oil accounted for most of the gain, with sales to China jumping 49 per cent to a record US$21.8 billion as shipments rose 27 per cent by volume and prices climbed 16.8 per cent. China took half of all the crude Brazil exported, nearly seven times the share of India, the next-largest buyer. Tensions in the Middle East and the risk of disruption to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz “increased the search for more stable suppliers, favouring Brazil, an important exporter of the commodity”, the council said in the report. Tehran effectively closed the strait after US and Israeli strikes on Iran began in late February, cutting off a route that carried more than half of China’s seaborne crude imports, according to ship-tracking firm Kpler. Chinese buyers increased purchases from Brazil even as China’s total crude imports fell 32 per cent in the second quarter, according to Chinese customs data cited by the US Energy Information Administration. Brazil’s crude exports to all markets grew 28.7 per cent to US$43 billion, with sales to India up 165 per cent. Oil now makes up 25.8 per cent of Brazilian exports to China, up 6.3 percentage points from a year earlier and second only to soybeans at 35.4 per cent. The shift has made Rio de Janeiro the largest exporting state to China, the report showed, as it supplied 89 per cent of the crude sold to the Chinese market. The nine-month figures also show the boom losing pace, since the council reported in July that exports to China had grown 22 per cent in the first half and that China had taken 54 per cent of Brazil’s crude. Gulf oil exports excluding Iran recovered to more than 81 per cent of pre-war levels in September after a US-Iran agreement in June, according to Kpler and Vortexa, although Iranian attacks on tankers have intensified this month. Beef was the biggest drag on Brazilian sales, falling 8.5 per cent to US$5.5 billion with volumes down 22 per cent, after Brazil filled its annual quota of 1.1 million tonnes under a Chinese safeguard. Shipments above it have paid a 55 per cent surtax since the start of this month, and September sales to China came to just US$68.3 million, compared with US$1.05 billion a year earlier. China fell to fifth place among buyers of Brazilian beef in September with 5.6 per cent of the total, the report showed, behind the United States at 21.5 per cent. Over the nine months, Brazilian exports to the United States fell 6.5 per cent, and the US took 9.6 per cent of Brazil’s sales abroad against 29.7 per cent for China. Electrified cars led the growth in imports from China, with purchases of plug-in hybrids up 89 per cent to US$2.87 billion and battery electric cars up 341 per cent to about US$2.4 billion. Together with conventional hybrids, they made up about a 10th of all Brazilian imports from China, and Chinese brands supplied 86 per cent of the electrified cars Brazil bought abroad. Monthly imports of the three categories collapsed from US$1.87 billion in June to US$22 million in July, when Brazil raised the import duty on them to 35 per cent, before recovering to US$449 million in September. BYD, the largest Chinese carmaker in Brazil, shipped large cargoes ahead of the increase and also assembles vehicles at a plant in Camacari, in Bahia state. The report also recorded the first results of Chinese market openings for Brazilian farm goods, with sorghum sales reaching US$170 million and China taking 95 per cent of Brazil’s exports of the grain. Exports of spodumene, a lithium-bearing mineral, rose 339 per cent to US$172.3 million, with 97 per cent going to China.

title: Prince Harry and Meghan in first joint outing since UK return: ‘great to be back!’
description: The couple’s quasi-royal visit could put the pair at odds with Buckingham Palace over their status while living back in Britain.
content: Britain’s Prince Harry and his wife on Thursday carried out their first joint engagement since their surprise move back to the UK in August, with Meghan telling well-wishers: “It’s great to be back.” King Charles’ 42-year-old younger son and Meghan, 45 – who left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud – were greeted with cheers as they arrived in the central English city of Nottingham. The couple then stopped to chat and joke with the crowd as well as pose for selfies, give hugs and accept flowers. The quasi-royal visit potentially puts the pair at odds with Buckingham Palace over their status while living back in Britain. The king made it clear in a letter released last month that their position was “akin to private citizens” with charitable interests rather than public figures and that they should not be addressed as his and her royal highness. Known formally as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, the last time Harry and Meghan appeared together at a public event in Britain was when they attended the late Queen Elizabeth’s funeral in September 2022. On Thursday, Meghan, dressed in a long burgundy winter coat and wearing her hair in a ponytail, at one point kissed a woman on the cheek after she presented her with a gift. Harry, in a dark suit and open-necked white shirt, bent down to speak to one youngster and told the crowd it was “very nice” to see everyone. The couple were in the city to visit three charities that support young people and local communities through music, film, sport and tackling food poverty. Following a spectacular falling out with the rest of the royal family, Harry and Meghan have sought to build bridges with Charles – but they remain estranged from Harry’s older brother and heir to the throne, Prince William. King Charles meanwhile visited Wales, where he addressed the Welsh parliament. Anti-monarchy protesters could be heard chanting “Not my King” and “Down, down, down with the Crown” as Charles and Queen Camilla arrived, according to reports. Charles, who was known as the Prince of Wales until his accession to the throne, has long had a close association with the country, one of the four territories that make up the United Kingdom. Harry and Meghan settled in California six years ago, but in a surprise move in August they returned to live in the UK with their two young children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five. The late Queen Elizabeth made it clear to Harry and Meghan before her death in 2022 that there was no “half-in/half-out” option under which they could pursue commercial ventures while being working royals. A letter issued last month by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior official in the Royal Household, said it was “well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the sovereign and are no longer working members of the royal family”. “Working royals” are members of the royal family who carry out official duties on behalf of the monarch. They receive administrative and other support from the Royal Household to do so. There are currently seven senior working royals – King Charles and Queen Camilla; son and heir Prince William and his wife Catherine, Princess of Wales; Charles’s sister Princess Anne, brother Edward and the latter’s wife Sophie. Other working royals include several of the late Queen Elizabeth’s cousins.

title: Firm accused of cost-cutting, false declarations over fire-safety parts in 48 lifts
description: Surprise inspections uncovered serious deficiencies in projects carried out by Taizoom Elevator (Hong Kong) at two estates, government says.
content: Hong Kong authorities have uncovered alleged corner-cutting and false declarations involving fire-safety components in a contractor’s replacement of 48 lifts at two public housing estates. The Electrical and Mechanical Services Department said on Thursday that surprise inspections had found serious deficiencies in projects carried out by Taizoom Elevator (Hong Kong) at Tsui Ping (North) Estate in Kwun Tong and Pok Hong Estate in Sha Tin. It said 39 lifts replaced between May 2025 and July this year were affected at Pok Hong Estate. Nine lifts replaced between February and July at Tsui Ping (North) Estate were also affected. The department said that although Taizoom had submitted fire-resistance test reports, inspectors found that it had only installed fire-resisting doors and not the corresponding door-frame components required before reporting the works as completed. Officials described the omission as a serious construction defect and a breach of regulatory requirements. The department said preliminary evidence suggested that Taizoom might have committed serious negligence or misconduct in relation to the lift work, and that it would take enforcement and regulatory action under the Lifts and Escalators Ordinance. It has also referred the case to police for further investigation, saying it would not rule out possible criminal offences involving fraud and false representations. But the department said the affected lifts remained safe for normal operation despite the missing components. It has ordered the contractor to reinspect all affected lifts and install the missing door-frame components at its own expense. Rectification work was expected to begin shortly and be completed within a month, it added. A citywide inspection of all lifts installed by Taizoom was under way, the department said. The Housing Authority said it was “highly concerned” about the incident and was maintaining close contact with the department. It vowed to “pursue the liabilities” of Taizoom.

title: Exclusive | EU open to creating ‘kill switch’ weapon to kick Chinese firms out of market
description: European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen also floats safeguards as member states back two-track strategy to tackle China shock.
content: Brussels is open to developing a powerful new trade weapon that could contain a kill switch that would quickly eject Chinese companies from the EU market, the bloc’s national leaders were told during a top-level meeting in the Belgian capital on Thursday. There was broad support among the 27 members for such a tool, first laid out in a French-German joint paper last week, with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen signalling that her trade team could get to work on developing it, according to people briefed on the talks. Von der Leyen presented the “kill switch” as an option during her opening presentation to the other leaders on Thursday, sources confirmed. As described in the joint paper, the instrument would allow Brussels to respond rapidly to systemic distortions and coercive behaviour, potentially immediately. It would grant dramatic new powers to the commission, the EU’s executive branch, which manages trade policy for the union. Furthermore, von der Leyen identified chemicals and industrial machinery as the top priority industries the EU needs to shield against Chinese imports during a meeting between the EU’s top leaders in Brussels on Thursday. She told members that the EU should consider quickly introducing safeguard measures, which can involve import quotas and tariffs, to shield these sectors from a wave of cut-price alternatives from China, according to people familiar with the discussion. Her motion was endorsed by influential member states, including France, Germany, Belgium and Denmark, while the wind turbine industry was also mentioned during the debate as one that needs intervention to alleviate pressure from Chinese imports, one of the people said. The bloc is currently running the numbers on these sectors using a monitoring mechanism it created to identify surges in imports. The discussion happened over a nearly two-hour lunch at the European Council summit in the Belgian capital, during which von der Leyen presented the results of several rounds of talks with the Chinese government, including an agreement that will see the EU cap imports of Chinese hybrid cars at 350,000 a year from 2027. In response, Beijing on Friday called for dialogue to address China-EU differences. “We hope the European side will abide by its commitments to openness and free trade, adhere to WTO rules, and avoid introducing protectionist and discriminatory policy measures,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a press conference. The South China Morning Post reported on Thursday that the EU was planning to open safeguard investigations in the chemicals, pharmaceuticals and machinery industries in the coming weeks. Politico first reported von der Leyen’s recommendation to EU leaders at the council summit. Multiple sources said that member states had lent “unanimous support” to the commission’s current approach – a two-pronged strategy of negotiating with Beijing while at the same time sharpening its own trade weapons. The dialogue is seen to have delivered results and working-level talks with Beijing continue. Meetings are set for their respective trade chiefs in January and March. But officials believe that the bloc cannot wait that long before acting to protect certain industries, sources said. This has led to a groundswell of support for more immediate intervention. Conclusions from the summit called for the commission to “urgently enhance the EU toolbox with new instruments to better address these imbalances”. In the meantime, safeguards are the preferred form of trade defence, since they can be implemented relatively quickly and can target more than one product at a time. Member states also rallied behind other elements in the joint paper, which urged a revamp of how the bloc uses its trade instruments, namely to make the process faster. Currently, it can take months or even years before a trade investigation is concluded, by which stage the damage is already done. The sum total is that members generally support further action against China, which could see a new spike in tensions, less than a week after the sides reached an agreement in Beijing that many thought would act as a salve. One of the people said that all of the member states who took the floor during the debate – during which the leaders dined on a main course of veal with a dessert of fig tart – spoke supportively of using caps to prevent a flood of Chinese exports in important sectors, such as that agreed in the hybrid car sector. “Fundamentally, I think it is a good idea to maintain a dialogue with China and see whether trade agreements can be reached,” said Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, arriving at the talks. “But as far as I can tell, China is not complying with the established rules governing trade between countries, and therefore Europe must be prepared to respond with the same firmness, if you will, as what we are witnessing from the outside.” Luxembourg’s premier Luc Frieden said the bloc needed to take “appropriate measures” against those countries who give their firms “unacceptable state aid”. “We have to protect our market while staying free-trade supporters, but free trade also means fair trade,” Frieden said. Speaking to the Financial Times, meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz signalled that his country’s dramatic pivot on China was here to stay. “We will widen the toolbox, we will open the toolbox, we will show the toolbox and we will make use of the toolbox if needed,” he told the newspaper.

title: Shackled Maduro defies judge, calls US torture charges ‘false accusations’
description: Ousted Venezuelan leader and his wife Cilia Flores face expanded indictment alleging beatings, electric shocks and abuse of three Americans.
content: Former Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro insisted in court on Thursday that newly unsealed torture allegations against him and his wife were “false accusations”. Maduro and Cilia Flores, both shackled at the ankles, were brought to court to face a rewritten indictment that expands from an initial set of drug trafficking charges to accuse them of leading a state-sponsored repression campaign that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans. Maduro twice defied a judge’s request that he enter a plea to the charges, instead condemning them through a courtroom interpreter as “false accusations and false testimony”. Irked, Judge Alvin Hellerstein took matters into his own hands, interjecting that “a plea of not guilty will be entered on behalf of Mr Maduro”. Flores was less combative. After saying that she had read through a version of the new indictment written in Spanish, she told the judge through the Spanish interpreter: “I am completely innocent. I am not guilty”. They were seized from their Caracas home by the US military in a nighttime raid in January. Their trial will begin June 14, 2027, two weeks later than previously set, according to a schedule approved by the judge Thursday. As they have in the past, Maduro and Flores listened to the proceedings through headphones carrying the voice of a courtroom translator. At times, the bespectacled Maduro looked through papers in front of him. When they entered the courtroom, Maduro waved to people in the gallery and shook hands with one of his lawyers, Barry Pollack, while Flores gave a peck on the cheek to Mark Donnelly, one of her lawyers. Pollack said when the charges were announced last week that Maduro, 63, denies them and “looks forward to his day in court”. Pollack agreed with the government’s request to move the trial to June 14. He told Hellerstein the new schedule was “very aggressive” given the new allegations, but added that he’s hopeful they’ll be able to stick to it. According to the rewritten indictment, Maduro oversaw a violent torture system that beat, asphyxiated, and delivered electric shocks to its victims. He is accused of personally recommending torture methods, receiving updates on specific victims’ treatment, and threatening to kill one prisoner’s child as a form of psychological torture. Flores, 70, a former attorney general, helped develop the repressive system and ordered the torture of some specific people, the indictment alleges. Maduro, who served as Venezuela’s president from 2013 until his capture in January, has been under investigation for years by the International Criminal Court over allegations of crimes against humanity, tied to his crackdown on opponents. He has always denied wrongdoing. Torture is a crime under international law and can be prosecuted outside of the nation where the abuse occurred and regardless of the victims’ nationality. But the prosecution of foreign officials in the US is exceedingly rare, having been tried only a few times, including against the son of former Liberian president Charles Taylor, Russians responsible for war crimes in Ukraine and a former prison warden in Bashar al-Assad’s Syria. Earlier this year, Maduro and his wife pleaded not guilty in the US drug case, which said they conspired to flood the US with cocaine. Their lawyers say the case should be dismissed on immunity grounds because they were the leader and first lady of a foreign country. The revised indictment covers allegations of torture stretching back to Maduro’s ascent to power in 2013, when he took over as president from his mentor Hugo Chavez, who died of cancer that year. The couple was scheduled to return to the courtroom for another pretrial hearing on December 17.

title: Hong Kong’s Hospital Authority appeals for liver donor for boy, 13
description: Boy is suffering from severe liver failure and urgently needs a transplant.
content: Hong Kong’s Hospital Authority has appealed to the public for a liver donation for a 13-year-old boy suffering from severe liver failure who urgently needs a transplant. The authority, which is also seeking help from mainland China, said on Thursday evening that the boy, being treated at Queen Mary Hospital in Pok Fu Lam, was now in a serious condition. “The patient has been experiencing severe hepatic failure and developed severe complications including recurrent hyperammonemia and cholangitis,” it said. “[He] is clinically assessed as requiring an urgent liver transplant and is listed at the top of the liver transplant waiting list for O+ blood group.” Hyperammonemia is elevated blood ammonia, which can poison the central nervous system, while cholangitis is inflammation of the bile ducts. The authority urged members of the public to proactively support organ donation and consider donating the organ of a deceased relative to “rekindle the lives of others”. Apart from searching for a suitable liver locally, the authority said it would also seek help from the mainland through the government given the boy’s condition. Under the cross-boundary organ donation and matching mechanism, an organ from a deceased donor on the mainland may be allocated to a Hong Kong patient if no suitable recipient is found on the mainland.

title: Singapore weighs legal action against companies over worsening transboundary haze
description: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong says the city state could invoke transboundary laws against firms responsible for Indonesian peatland fires.
content: Singapore is looking into which companies may be responsible for the forest and peatland fires in Indonesia that have caused the worsening haze, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Thursday. “Where warranted, we will take action under Singapore’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, and explore joint action with other countries,” he said in a social media post. The haze situation was worsened by the extended dry period, Wong added. Singapore had offered its assistance to Indonesia and would continue working closely with the country and other Association of Southeast Asian Nations partners to address the issue, he said. N95 and equivalent masks are being distributed to vulnerable Singaporeans, while air-conditioned shelters are being made available at community clubs and selected residents’ network and residents’ committee centres. “We will ensure support is available to those who need it,” he said. “We cannot control the weather or winds, or what happens beyond our borders. But we will do everything we can to protect Singaporeans, while working with our neighbours to address the haze’s underlying causes,” Wong added. This story was first published by CNA

title: AFC Champions League 2: Hong Kong’s Tai Po ‘cross a line’ but fail to tame Lion City Sailors
description: Singaporean visitors too slick and smart for tenacious hosts, while local league champions Kitchee claim precious away point.
content: Streetwise Lion City Sailors condemned Tai Po to a 1-0 AFC Champions League 2 defeat at Mong Kok Stadium on Thursday, but victorious boss Mark Jackson accused the hosts of “crossing a line” in their attempts to ruffle the Singaporean team. A husk of the side that was unbeaten at home in last season’s competition, following a summer firesale, Tai Po nevertheless ran themselves into the ground in a vain attempt to recover from the blow of Matthias Phaeton’s strike shortly after half-time. While Lee Chi-kin, the Tai Po head coach, said that in the context of their limited resources his team “did a good job”, the recently-appointed Jackson believed Lion City’s victory would “do wonders for our belief and confidence”. It was a second straight win for the new boss, after he began his reign with one draw and one loss. Lion City trail Adelaide United by two points at the top of ACL2 Group F, after the Australians beat BG Pathum United 2-1 for their second win from as many matches. Thai team Pathum have one point, while Tai Po are yet to get off the mark. “It’s a platform for us to go on in this competition,” said Jackson, the former Leeds United player and coach who won the ACL2 in its previous AFC Cup guise in charge of Central Coast Mariners two years ago. “It takes a lot to win it, but I truly believe I’m at a club with the resources, players and staff to have a real go at it. “You always want to play your type of football, to be free flowing and score lots of goals, but sometimes you have to dig in, and our players can do that when it gets a little bit ugly.” Lion City made all the running before half-time but repeatedly ran aground on a disciplined, well-organised Tai Po defensive wall. The visitors’ midfielder, Song Ui-young, came closest to breaking the deadlock when his drifted 32nd-minute effort from distance clipped the top of the bar. On the back foot immediately after the restart, Tai Po conceded when Phaeton converted following a corner from former France under-19 international midfielder Giovanni Haag. “Set plays can be a point of difference in these types of competitions …. We put a lot of emphasis on them, and we’ll continue to do that,” Jackson said. Substitute Wallisson Bahia ignited a home rally, the Brazilian forward first curling narrowly wide, then sliding over a cross that the outstanding Diogo Costa slammed off the line after goalkeeper Victor Aznar was unsure with his handling. As Tai Po got their blood up, Jackson and his staff were visibly furious over a handful of enthusiastic challenges that either went entirely unpunished, or resulted in free-kicks without the miscreant being booked. “They can put teams under pressure and be very physical, and, for me, they crossed the line on occasions, but we dealt with that well” Jackson said. “Tai Po will cause problems for the other teams in this group.” Asked where Tai Po had strayed too far, Jackson said “I don’t mind physicality, I’m from Leeds. I just think it needs to be managed a little bit better. I was proud of how my players handled the situation, they stuck to it and didn’t get carried away.” Lee disagreed with Jackson’s take. “I don’t know why he would think that,” he said, pointing to the solitary booking his team received. “We just tried our best to run and to cover positions.” A Tai Po spokesman said the club “agreed football should be played physically … but you didn’t see any arguments during the match”. Left-back Costa lashed over when Phaeton gave him the chance to put the match to bed. Soon after, it was the turn of Antonio Mance to sky an opportunity from close range following a right-wing cross along the floor from fellow substitute Ryhan Stewart. “There are easier ways to get three points but all that matters is that we did,” Jackson said. Guadeloupe international forward Phaeton added: “The opponent gave us a strong game, they’re a really strong team. But we responded to the physical part, and we’re happy to take the three points.” Lee, meanwhile, “applauded my players” for their gutsy performance. “They played their hearts out and didn’t give up,” he said. “Our opponents cost more, and they’re more powerful. You can’t say you’re happy when you lose, but we understand where we are with our squad.” Lee also downplayed the paltry 976 attendance for an early evening kick-off. “In Hong Kong, if you can leave the office at 6pm, you’re very lucky,” he said. Elsewhere, Kitchee claimed a creditable 1-1 draw at Kuching City. Currently second in the Malaysia Super League, Kuching had a dream start when Kitchee keeper Pong Cheuk-hei put through his own net after two minutes. A murderous Everton Camargo drive 12 minutes later secured the local league champions a valuable point. They are second in Group H on two points, after Phnom Penh Crown won 2-1 at Gangwon FC for a second straight victory. Gangwon and Kuching both have one point.

title: Trump scraps plan to live-stream Fort Hood shooter’s execution by firing squad
description: US president says former US Army psychiatrist Nidal Malik Hasan’s execution will proceed, with victims’ immediate families allowed to attend.
content: US President Donald Trump on Thursday cancelled plans to live-stream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan, reversing a Pentagon initiative that drew political and religious criticism. Trump said Hasan’s execution by firing squad would proceed as scheduled, but would not be broadcast. The Pentagon has set the execution for December 3. “He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others at the Texas military base in November 2009. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth outlined the plan in an interview with conservative broadcaster Real America’s Voice, reported on October 8. Speaking aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, he said the execution should be available to watch “because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things”. The Pentagon issued a statement later that day confirming that it intended to live-stream the execution. In his Thursday post, Trump defended the potential deterrent value of broadcasting the execution, even as he ruled it out. “I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan,” he wrote. But he added, “many very good and well-meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device”. Trump said immediate family members of the victims could witness the execution in person if they wished. Critics warned that broadcasting the execution could fuel radicalisation. The proposal also drew opposition from the Catholic Church, human rights groups and the United Nations. Senator Jack Reed, the senior Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, warned that a live stream would give Hasan a global platform, calling the proposal “a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters”. Archbishop Paul S. Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, denounced the plan as “a barbaric promotion of a culture of death”. Amnesty International USA said broadcasting the killing would compound its cruelty, while the UN human rights office warned that it would violate the absolute prohibition on torture. Vice-President J.D. Vance had previously expressed doubt that the broadcast would happen and said he would not watch it. “I don’t know that that’s actually going to happen,” Vance said when asked earlier this month how a public execution would comport with his Christian faith. Hasan, who held the rank of major, opened fire in a medical building where soldiers were preparing for deployment on November 5, 2009. He said he wanted to prevent troops from going to Afghanistan and killing fellow Muslims, according to the Associated Press. A military judge barred him from presenting that argument as a defence during his 2013 trial.

title: China is a beacon of global embryo research, says scientist on return from US to lead lab
description: Wu Jun joins Hangzhou’s Westlake University to advance organ regeneration and AI-driven embryo research.
content: Leading life scientist Wu Jun, who recently left the United States to return to his homeland, believes many of the world’s top embryo researchers are now working in China. Wu, well known for his stem cell research, particularly related to the stem cell-derived embryo model, is speaking in an office at Westlake University, in Hangzhou in the eastern province of Zhejiang. Some of his belongings remain in bags placed haphazardly on a nearby cabinet, waiting to be unpacked. “This is just a temporary office; my lab and office are still being set up,” Wu said. He officially joined his new institution as chair professor of stem cell biology and regenerative medicine a month ago despite being promoted to a tenured professorship at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Centre (UT Southwestern) earlier this year. His former employer made sincere efforts to retain him, including considering a counter-offer, but he politely declined. “My decision to return had already been made; no amount of money would have kept me there,” he said. On the Westlake website, his new employer lists Wu’s achievements, including his “significant contributions” to basic and translational research in pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) – undifferentiated cells capable of generating any cell or tissue in the body. He is also praised for his leading pioneering efforts in the generation of interspecies chimeras – experimental organisms containing cells from various species – and stem cell-based embryo models. After more than two decades in the US where he trained and established himself, the 49-year-old biologist is riding the crest of a wave in the scientific community: accomplished academics moving from the US to China. A factor cementing his decision was the concentration of talent within this research field in China. “Including those trained in our lab and other labs, among the researchers working on stem cell-based embryo models, I think many are now in China,” he said. As the head of a leading laboratory in this field, he noted that many of the postdoctoral researchers he trained in Texas had returned to China and were operating at a world-class level. “China has an obvious advantage in conducting research in fields such as human embryonic development, stem cell-based embryo and organ models,” he said. More broadly, Wu said, Westlake University had attracted a large number of young, dynamic and innovative scientists trained in many of the world’s most prestigious laboratories. “They bring these ideas, knowledge and so on back to the university, which creates a vibrant scientific energy,” he said. China’s emphasis on cutting-edge life sciences was another factor prompting him to leave the excellent conditions in Texas, he said, adding that China offered a more supportive environment for human embryo model research. Born in Shandong in 1977, Wu received his bachelor’s degree in clinical medicine from the Shandong University school of medicine. In 2003, during the study-abroad boom of the early 2000s, he headed to the US to obtain a PhD in life sciences from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville. He then completed postdoctoral training at the University of Southern California and the San Diego-based, independent Salk Institute. In 2017, during his tenure at Salk, his team’s creation of the world’s first human-pig chimeric embryos attracted global attention. In the experiment, human stem cells were injected into a pig embryo – although of the 2,075 embryos implanted into a sow, only 186 continued to develop to the 28-day stage. In 2018, Wu joined UT Southwestern’s molecular biology department as an assistant professor. The laboratory led by the rising star scientist consistently announced scientific advances, resulting in his promotion to associate professor in 2023 and, just three years later, to full professor. Wu gained several international accolades for his scientific contributions. Among them, he received the Outstanding Young Investigator Award from the International Society for Stem Cell Research in 2024. He received a Discovery and Innovation Grant Award from the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and was named a 2021 Robertson Stem Cell Investigator by The New York Stem Cell Foundation. In his temporary office, the biologist recalled that his connection with Westlake University began eight years ago, just as he was joining UT Southwestern. Around the same time, he learned that his colleague, Yu Hongtao – a leading scientist who had been at the American university for nearly two decades – had chosen to join the new research-focused university in Hangzhou. In later years, at the invitation of Yu and other academics, Wu delivered academic seminars at Westlake on several occasions, which he said deepened his understanding of the institution. By this year, he felt the timing was right to accept a full-time position, taking into account his career trajectory as well as the support and expectations of his family. At his new institution, Wu will lead a laboratory engaging in stem cell embryology and chimera biology. As a chair professor – the highest rank in the university’s professorial hierarchy – he is setting up a laboratory and expects to be joined by dozens of doctoral and postdoctoral researchers. He said he would continue to explore the most fundamental scientific questions, such as how life develops at a molecular and cellular level. This includes using pluripotent stem cells to build in vitro models of early human embryonic development. He aims to aid the understanding of biological development, conquer diseases and realise long-term visions, such as organ regeneration. His team will continue to tackle complex challenges, including research on human-animal chimeras. If successful, this could eventually help scientists develop human organs in animals for transplant. His new laboratory is also expected to integrate AI into stem cell research, using algorithms to accelerate the screening process for organ generation.

title: Blast simulation, university probes, robotics fine, AI spies: 7 US-China relations reads

title: Hong Kong loses record 40 kindergartens as birth rate drops, women wait to have kids
description: City down to 930 kindergartens as student population declines and age of first-time mums rises to record high.
content: Hong Kong suffered a record net loss of 40 kindergartens this year amid a shrinking student population and as the median age of women giving birth to their first child rose to its highest yet, according to official figures. In its overview of preschools released on Thursday, the Education Bureau revealed that 930 kindergartens were currently operating in Hong Kong, down from roughly 970 in the previous school year. While some new kindergartens were launched, the net decrease stood at 40, the highest on record. Each of the past four academic years witnessed a net decrease of about 20 preschools. The situation reflects the low birth rate in 2022, which was the second-lowest on record with just 32,500 babies born. They entered kindergarten in the previous school year. Kentville Kindergarten is among the schools that have closed, with the prestigious private institution in Kowloon Tong citing low birth rates, emigration of young families and staff retirement as the reasons. The future for preschools appears bleak, as annual births remain low and are expected to hit their lowest point this year. According to the official figures, Hong Kong recorded fewer than 30,000 births over 12 months for the first time between July 2025 and June 2026. The city’s midyear population, however, edged up by 0.3 per cent to 7,518,300, or 19,400 more compared with the same period last year. The survival of government-subsidised kindergartens heavily relies on the number of pupils they admit, as headcounts are tied to government subsidies. Authorities introduced 11 measures to encourage childbirth in the city leader’s policy address last month, including extending a HK$20,000 (US$2,564) newborn cash incentive for three more years and launching a progressive reward scheme that raises the incentive to HK$30,000 for the second child and subsequent ones. To survive, some kindergartens previously offering only half-day modes have started offering full-day sessions to lure working parents. The Census and Statistics Department recently announced that the median age of women having their first child stood at 33.1 last year, up from 32.8 in 2024. It was the first time the figure exceeded 33. Between 2000 and 2025, the median age underwent a sustained upwards trend, rising from 29.3 years in 2000 to 33.1 years in 2025, an overall increase of 3.8 years, or 13 per cent. It also coincided with couples waiting until later in life to marry. The median age for a first marriage stands at 32 for men and 31.3 for women, compared with 30 and 27.3, respectively, in 2000, with females delaying marriage much more than males. Lawmaker Judy Chan Kapui has urged the government to set up a high-ranking working group to coordinate birth-boosting policies. “If there is more coordination of the related policies, bureaus would not only think of their areas when devising their policies, but also care about the policy impact on births,” she said. Chan also said young generations already had a perception that “not having children is the norm”, urging the government to launch a citywide campaign to change that view.

title: Alibaba sets sights on record-breaking Singles’ Day with 1 million brands joining festival
description: Over 70 million products are also expected to feature this year, as the e-commerce giant expands Qwen-powered tools and pushes international sales.
content: Alibaba Group Holding is gearing up for its annual Singles’ Day shopping festival on major online marketplaces Taobao and Tmall, with the company expecting a record one million global brands to take part this year. Pre-sales for the event open on Thursday, followed by the formal sale next Tuesday. The company projects more than 70 million products to feature, also a record for the festival. Created by Alibaba in 2009, Singles’ Day has grown into the world’s largest online shopping festival. Also known as Double 11, it tapped into a trend among young single people to buy gifts for themselves on November 11, a date chosen for its four ones. What began as a one-day sale has since turned into a huge weeks-long promotion spanning multiple platforms and is seen as an important barometer of domestic consumption in China. Alibaba said it was combining discounts and coupons that could lead to savings of up to 28 per cent in some cases. It is also giving out tens of billions of yuan worth of coupons specifically designed for its 88VIP membership programme, its highest-spending consumer group, which had about 64 million members as of June. This year’s event will feature deeper integration of the company’s flagship artificial intelligence model, Qwen, across its e-commerce ecosystem. A Qwen-powered shopping assistant launched in May helps users compare products, virtually try on clothing and select promotional offers, according to the company. The launch followed the company’s first large-scale deployment of generative AI on Taobao and Tmall during the same event in 2025, when it integrated large language models into core search and recommendation engines. Another trend this year is the increasing presence of overseas brands, with 60,000 new merchants joining the event for the first time. US tech giant Apple is among the marquee participants and is set to begin accepting pre-orders for its latest foldable device, the iPhone Duo, on Tmall on Friday. Alibaba said the new iPhone 18 Pro series would be eligible for a 300 yuan (US$44.82) “surprise coupon” from October 20. One of the newcomers is US yoga apparel brand Alo, which opened its first online store in China on Tmall in August. Separately, Taobao announced a comprehensive upgrade to its official international logistics system as it seeks to navigate geopolitical and tariff uncertainties while expanding overseas. Leveraging a network of more than 600 partners in more than 200 countries and regions, the e-commerce platform plans to speed up cross-border delivery times to as little as one day and replace consolidated shipping with direct delivery. Taobao also pledged that overseas customers using its official logistics services would not face hidden fees and fluctuating surcharges, though tariffs could change and other issues could arise during shipping. “Costs may fluctuate during the process, but the platform will absorb those fluctuations,” said Phil Ding Hongwei, vice-president of Alibaba and head of logistics at Taobao Tmall World, at a briefing on Thursday in Hong Kong. Despite persistent trade tensions, Taobao said it would continue to embrace globalisation as a core strategy. The logistics upgrade was expected to cover all major markets spanning from Singapore to Canada, according to Ye Tian, general manager of Taobao Tmall World. Meanwhile, rival JD.com already kicked off its Singles’ Day promotions on Monday. The company said on Thursday that the number of buyers on the first day saw double-digit growth from a year earlier. Alibaba owns the South China Morning Post.

title: Chinese referee Ma Ning recounts ‘harrowing’ trip to officiate match with Cristiano Ronaldo
description: AFC Champions League Elite fixture between Al-Nassr and Neftchi Fergana goes ahead despite attack on airport, disruptions in Saudi Arabia.
content: Chinese referee Ma Ning shared details about his “harrowing” journey after officiating an AFC Champions League Elite fixture in Saudi Arabia on social media on Wednesday. Amid escalating tensions in the region following a recent attack on Riyadh’s international airport, the six-member Chinese officiating crew led by Ma completed their match assignment despite severe travel disruptions and uncomfortable conditions in the host city. The officials were in Riyadh for the AFC Champions League Elite match between Cristiano Ronaldo’s Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr and Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana on Tuesday. Following the fixture, the crew travelled overnight by road, completing a seven-hour journey to Doha, Qatar, before boarding a flight back to China. Expressing relief at returning to the “embrace of the great motherland”, Ma said he felt deeply “at ease” and thanked supporters, describing the mission as “both fraught with twists and harrowing”. The journey was plagued by complications from the start. The departing flight was delayed, and then it was unable to land in Riyadh due to an incident on the ground. The plane was diverted but its next destination was not accepting flights, forcing it to divert and eventually land at a third airport. Once on the ground, the officials then encountered more complications and split into two groups to travel by road for up to nine hours, arriving on the eve of the match. The problems, however, continued on matchday. “Just 15 minutes before the match, we received an emergency alert on our mobile phones,” Ma recalled. “The match commissioner then notified us that the match was delayed for security reasons. Around 45 minutes later, we received notice that the game could proceed, warmed up again, and started the match.” Operating under considerable uncertainty, the Chinese team, which also included assistant referees Zhou Fei and Luo Zheng, fourth official Zhang Lei, VAR Fu Ming and AVAR Du Jianxin, carried out their duties. Al-Nassr won the match 3-1, with Ronaldo on the scoresheet and Ma handing out four yellow cards and one red. After the final whistle, the team opted against staying in Riyadh, leaving immediately overland. “After the match ended, we decided to travel directly by vehicle from the stadium to an international airport in a neighbouring country,” Ma said. “After a seven-hour journey, we reached the neighbouring country’s international airport and returned smoothly to Shanghai.” Reflecting on the decision to press ahead with the assignment, Ma noted the team had legitimate grounds to withdraw both before departure and following the flight diversions. “However, we still decided to travel to the match venue to complete this officiating assignment,” he said. “Once we accepted the appointment, we had a responsibility to see it through. At the same time, we wanted the world to see that Chinese referees are professionally capable and trustworthy.” Ma offered special thanks to the Chinese Embassy in Saudi Arabia, the Chinese Football Association, his family and supporters, noting that embassy personnel remained in constant communication from the moment the officials arrived in Riyadh until their safe return. “We do not live in a peaceful era, but we live in a peaceful country, so we must cherish the fine life we have today,” Ma said. “At the same time, we pay tribute to our revolutionary martyrs who created such a fine environment for us.” Saudi Arabia is set to stage the Asian Cup for the first time ⁠in 2027, a key test ⁠before the 2034 World Cup. The tournament is scheduled to kick off on January 7 across eight venues in three cities – Riyadh, ‌Jeddah and Al-Khobar. Asian Football Confederation president Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said they were in “no hurry to make a decision” on whether to postpone the tournament or not. “We can wait until the ‌end ‌of November. Things can change very quickly for better or worse in the region and it is a question of seeing what happens,” ‌he said. “If we need to make a decision then we will, but we ⁠could move back a year to 2028 if we need to. But at the moment we are monitoring the situation and everything ⁠is on schedule.”

title: DeepSeek offers user refunds after suffering another major outage
description: Chinese AI firm apologises and offers one-week refund after its chatbot and API services went offline for nearly five hours.
content: Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek apologised and promised compensation to users after its services suffered a nearly five-hour outage on Thursday. DeepSeek will issue users a full refund for any consumption between October 8 and October 14 in the form of credits, according to a notice posted on the Hangzhou-based start-up’s application programming interface (API) platform. DeepSeek’s namesake chatbot and API services for its V4 Pro and V4.1 Flash models went offline on Thursday morning, affecting users globally, before being restored over four hours and 50 minutes later at around 1pm. Some users turned to social media to share the error messages they had encountered when trying to use DeepSeek, such as “server temporarily unavailable”. “We immediately launched a comprehensive investigation and thorough rectification effort focused on service stability, and have comprehensively reviewed and eliminated single points of dependency to resolutely prevent similar issues from recurring,” DeepSeek said in the notice, without elaborating on the cause of the incident. “We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience and disruption this may have caused.” The incident came as the company faces mounting infrastructure pressure amid surging compute demand. DeepSeek is looking to expand its teams and computing infrastructure as competition intensifies, with a plan to add about 1 gigawatt of computing capacity in China’s northern Inner Mongolia autonomous region, according to a Bloomberg report. DeepSeek has faced recurring service disruptions, but the latest outage was one of the most severe it has experienced in recent months. The platform also suffered a major disruption in March that lasted for around 12 hours, affecting hundreds of millions of users. In late January last year, shortly after the then little-known lab released its R1 reasoning model and made it free globally, DeepSeek was hit by denial-of-service attacks meant to overwhelm its servers and bandwidth with a flood of internet traffic. The company described them as “large-scale malicious attacks” at the time.

title: Canada, Singapore reaffirm China trade ties amid global push for self-sufficiency
description: The two countries push back against global fragmentation, telling a New Delhi forum that key partnerships with Beijing must continue.
content: Canada and Singapore are among the countries that remain committed to strengthening trade ties with China, despite growing global fragmentation and a push by governments towards greater self-sufficiency, officials from both countries said on Wednesday at an economic forum in New Delhi. Canada’s minister of international trade Maninder Sidhu said China was the country’s second-largest trading partner and highlighted opportunities for cooperation in areas where the two economies had complementary strengths, including China’s technology and Canada’s agricultural sectors. “If you look at what China has in terms of energy storage technologies, that’s where Canada is very interested,” Sidhu said in a panel discussion titled “The Self-Sufficiency Scramble” at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, held in New Delhi from Tuesday to Thursday. “There are key areas where we have partnerships with China we continue to build on,” he said, pointing to Canada’s agricultural sector that supplied “a great deal of canola or beef”, among other products, to the Chinese market. Singapore’s Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, also minister for trade and industry, echoed that view, saying countries needed to maintain economic ties at a time when geopolitical tensions were increasingly dividing the global economy. “It’s important for countries in the world to continue to engage with one another, even as the world has become increasingly fragmented,” Gan said, reaffirming the city state’s commitment to collaborating with China. “Singapore and China will continue to have a very good working relationship. We continue to have a very strong economic cooperation in all aspects of the economy.” Gan said, adding that Singapore also collaborated strategically with other countries, such as India, in areas including semiconductors. Their remarks underscored the difficulties of disentangling global supply chains that are deeply interconnected, even as trade disruption, geopolitical frictions and concerns over economic security push governments to reduce their dependence on foreign suppliers and seek self-sufficiency. I don’t think technology will remain the reserve of only one or a few countries Piyush Goyal, Indian commerce and industry minister Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman at Bharti Enterprises, an Indian multinational conglomerate headquartered in New Delhi, cautioned against overreliance on a single source – such as China – for critical supply chains. “For a long period of time, I think the world let China become very strong in almost everything, from pharmaceuticals to the most critical components of the automobiles to electronics,” Mittal said at a separate forum panel held on Wednesday. “Everybody is very happy that China produces high quality at low cost,” Mittal said, adding that interdependencies were becoming a “big question mark”. Piyush Goyal, India’s commerce and industry minister, argued that technological capabilities would not remain concentrated in a handful of economies indefinitely. He said that developing alternative supply chains would require cooperation, rather than each country attempting to replicate an entire industrial ecosystem. “I don’t think technology will remain the reserve of only one or a few countries.” Some countries could contribute talent, others specialised in equipment or components, while still others could provide the products and services needed to support commercial development, he added. Goyal said that India was open to all countries around the world as long as the geopolitical situation did not deteriorate. Though there were past concerns related to China, he said, the two countries were currently working on developing their relations. Singapore’s Gan added that even in an increasingly fragmented world, countries that found ways to cooperate would be better positioned to navigate potential disruptions ahead. “If you are able to do that, you will have a better future for all of us,” he said.

title: Opinion | Young Americans are key for the US to better understand China
