It asked the top court to halt the revision of electoral rolls, investigate alleged irregularities and examine whether Kumar acted without the approval of his fellow commissioners. The court is expected to hear the petition along with other cases stemming from the protests on Thursday, including restrictions, detentions and alleged police excesses. “We are not going to stop. We will go to the end goal,” Congress leader Rahul Gandhi told reporters after meeting opposition lawmakers on Tuesday. “How we will get there, we can’t tell you because that would spoil the surprise, and we want to keep it interesting for the country.” The ongoing dispute adds to political tensions for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government ahead of key state elections, including next year’s vote in Uttar Pradesh, India’s most populous state. Modi has not publicly commented on the latest protests. His Bharatiya Janata Party has defended the voter-roll revision and accused opposition parties of attempting to undermine democratic institutions. The opposition cannot say that the Election Commission is doing a good job and that “elections are perfect” when they win, but claim that “elections are rigged” when they do not, BJP leader and Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal told reporters on Tuesday. The issue is also drawing support from farmers’ groups. Samyukt Kisan Morcha, a coalition of farmers’ organisations, announced nationwide demonstrations on October 23 at district and subdistrict levels. The controversy erupted in late September after an investigation by The Indian Express reported that Kumar had disregarded concerns raised by the other two election commissioners over the revision of voter lists. More than 130 million names were removed from draft electoral rolls, fuelling allegations by opposition parties that eligible voters were being excluded. The Election Commission has denied allegations of wrongdoing, saying its decisions were unanimous and that differing views among commissioners are part of the decision-making process. The protests add to the challenges facing Modi’s government after thousands of students took to the streets in July over exam irregularities, culminating in the education minister’s resignation. The unrest also comes at a difficult moment for the economy, with the government seeking to bolster investor confidence and boost growth. Indian equities have slumped, while the rupee is among Asia’s worst-performing currencies this year.

title: Commuters stranded as track fire disrupts MTR services in Hong Kong
description: MTR Corp spokesman says insulating rubber component of rail switch at Lam Tin station caught fire, likely due to short circuit.
content: A fire near an MTR track halted train services between Kwun Tong and Tiu Keng Leng stations during the evening rush hour in Hong Kong on Tuesday, leaving commuters stranded on packed platforms and concourses. Services along the Kwun Tong line gradually resumed at roughly 6.40pm after the fire was extinguished, the MTR Corporation said. The fire, reported along the Whampoa-bound line near Lam Tin station, led to the suspension of services at four stations: Kwun Tong, Lam Tin, Yau Tong and Tiu Keng Leng, as crowds began to swell from about 6pm. The station was immediately closed, and hundreds of commuters were evacuated. Frustrated passengers took to social media to share photos of congested concourses and platform bottlenecks, reporting long queues to exit the stations. A police spokesman said station staff reported a fire on the tracks at about 5.42pm. During the incident, trains continued to run between Kwun Tong and Whampoa stations at four-minute intervals on the Kwun Tong line. Free shuttle buses were arranged between Kwun Tong, Lam Tin and Yau Tong stations. An MTR Corp spokesman said an insulating rubber component of a track turnout at Lam Tin station caught fire at around 5.30pm, likely due to a short circuit. A turnout, commonly called a rail switch, is an installation that allows trains to change from one track to another by guiding their wheels along either a straight or diverging route. Following inspections by firefighters and comprehensive safety checks, and after the temperature of the device had cooled to a suitable level, Kwun Tong line services began to return to normal at about 6.30pm. The company vowed to conduct a thorough investigation into the cause of the fire. While firefighters sent to the scene found no flames or smoke, footage provided by the company showed orange-yellow flames and light white smoke billowing from the gap between the track switch and the ground. Authorities confirmed that no injuries were reported, and following an inspection, police and fire personnel concluded that there were no suspicious circumstances surrounding the incident. During the disruption, MTR Corp staff were deployed to assist passengers, while personnel investigated the incident and worked to restore services.

title: Why Samsung, SK Hynix and CXMT shares are under pressure despite strong AI demand
description: Investors seem to be weighing strong earnings prospects against the risk of slower memory price growth as supply catches up with demand.
content: A sharp sell-off in Asian memory chip stocks this week signals growing investor doubts over whether the sector’s AI-driven profit boom can last, even as soaring prices drive strong quarterly earnings across the sector. Shares in market leaders Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plunged in Seoul on Tuesday, extending a days-long slide that has also swept up Chinese rival ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). Samsung and SK Hynix closed down 7.4 per cent and 10.1 per cent, respectively. The companies have fallen about 16 per cent and 22 per cent, respectively, over the past five trading sessions. Together, they account for about half the weight of South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index, which closed 5.5 per cent lower after falling more than 7 per cent intraday. In Shanghai, CXMT, China’s leading dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) maker, closed down 2.8 per cent at 46.99 yuan (US$7.01), extending its drop since the close before China’s National Day holiday to about 14 per cent. Analysts said investors were becoming less confident that memory chipmakers could sustain their windfall profits amid longer-term supply risks and valuation pressures. Morgan Stanley analyst Shawn Kim wrote in a Sunday note that investors were looking beyond the current surge in earnings, supported by demand for AI-related chips. “We think the easy money is past,” he wrote. The recent rally may also have encouraged some investors to lock in gains. Kiwoom Securities strategist Han Ji-young wrote in a market commentary on Tuesday that foreign investors were reducing their holdings after a strong run in South Korean equities. The retrenchment came despite strong financial reports. Samsung’s shares fell on Thursday even after the tech giant forecast quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won (US$79.9 billion), broadly matching market expectations. That pressure quickly spread to the United States, where chipmaker Micron lost 3.9 per cent and Sandisk fell 6 per cent on Monday. The two stocks were down a further 2.4 per cent and 2.8 per cent, respectively, in early Tuesday premarket trading. The change in sentiment has also affected CXMT, whose shares surged as much as 614 per cent above their July offer price to a record 61.80 yuan in mid-August. By Tuesday’s close, however, the shares were down about 20 per cent from their September 23 close. Analysts said CXMT could be particularly exposed if memory price growth cooled. Visible Alpha, part of S&P Global Market Intelligence, forecast that CXMT’s average selling price for conventional DRAM chips would rise 206 per cent this year, far outpacing projected shipment growth of 79 per cent. Research firm SemiAnalysis estimated that CXMT’s cost of producing each bit of DDR5 memory remained more than 30 per cent higher than that of its three largest global rivals, while high-bandwidth memory (HBM) contributed little to its revenue. Slower price increases could limit CXMT’s margin gains, even if it continues to sell more chips. At the same time, CXMT’s rapid expansion could pose a growing challenge to its overseas rivals. Counterpoint Research estimated that the company’s share of global DRAM revenue reached 10 per cent in the second quarter, up from 4 per cent a year earlier. CXMT also announced over the weekend that it aimed to introduce a new DDR5 server-memory product by the end of the year using a 4F square cell architecture. The next-generation design is intended to reduce the area of a memory cell, potentially allowing more memory to fit on the chip. If the company is successful, the technology could strengthen its position in server memory, a lucrative segment long dominated by Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron. Tesla CEO Elon Musk weighed in on China’s prospects in the memory industry. In a post on X on Monday, he said Chinese manufacturers expand production rapidly once they have learned to make a product. “Their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined”, he wrote. Musk added that China appeared to be making rapid progress in low-power memory standards such as LPDDR5 and LPDDR6, while suggesting that newer HBM architectures would prove harder to master. However, market watchers cautioned against assuming CXMT posed an immediate threat. Han of Kiwoom Securities said the company’s planned server product had not entered mass production, while its manufacturing yields, performance and customer qualification remained unverified. Near-term market supplies also remain tight. Market intelligence firm TrendForce expected conventional DRAM contract prices to rise by a further 10 to 15 per cent this quarter, albeit at a slower pace. Morgan Stanley expected memory prices to remain firm through 2027, with increases slowing as supply caught up with demand or clients paused orders to digest existing inventory. Investors are now looking to Samsung’s full earnings announcement on October 29 for more details on memory-supply arrangements for 2027 and HBM pricing. Morgan Stanley analysts said those indicators would matter more to the company’s stock than its preliminary profit figures.

title: 179 reports of people trapped in lifts after power dip in Hong Kong
description: Fire Services Department says dip affected parts of Kowloon and New Territories, leading to multiple lift incidents and fire alarms.
content: Authorities received nearly 180 reports of people being trapped in lifts after a brief voltage dip in CLP Power’s network tripped building safety mechanisms in various districts across Hong Kong on Tuesday, with three elderly women hospitalised after feeling unwell. The Fire Services Department said that from 1.10pm to 3pm, it received 179 reports of people trapped in lifts and 40 fire alarms going off in parts of Kowloon and the New Territories. Residential and commercial buildings, hospitals, shopping centres, MTR stations and school campuses were affected. Four women aged between 68 and 71 reported feeling unwell, acting deputy chief fire officer Yung Wai-ming said at a press briefing. Three of them were sent to hospital, as they experienced discomfort and shortness of breath. One experienced symptoms of high blood pressure. “We sent some vehicles from other districts to help with the cases, which is why the handling time took longer. For those affected by fire alarms, the longest [wait] was 49 minutes,” Yung said. “For people trapped in lifts, the longest rescue time was one hour and 20 minutes.” Among the areas affected were Sha Tin, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hung Hom, Yau Tong, Po Lam, Kwun Tong, Kwai Chung, Mong Kok, Cheung Sha Wan, Tai Po and Tsuen Wan. In a reply to the South China Morning Post, CLP Power – which supplies electricity to Kowloon, the New Territories and most outlying islands – said the voltage drop occurred on a 400,000-volt power line connecting Lai Chi Kok to Tsz Wan Shan in Kowloon, adding that there was “no interruption to power supply”. “During the voltage dip, some customers may have experienced dimming or flickering of lights; certain electrical appliances that are sensitive to voltage fluctuations may have ceased operation due to the activation of protective devices,” a spokesman said, adding that an investigation was under way.

title: SHKP reopens former Crowne Plaza hotel as luxury ‘urban resort’ in Tseung Kwan O
description: The Royal Garden Kowloon East has been completely overhauled to meet the changing needs of travellers in Hong Kong, developer says.
content: The new Royal Garden Kowloon East hotel has undergone far more than an extensive renovation; it has been completely overhauled to become an “urban resort” in the heart of Tseung Kwan O, according to the hotel’s owner. Developer Sun Hung Kai Properties (SHKP) had transformed the former Crowne Plaza “from a traditional business hotel into a brand-new urban resort experience” to cater to a new generation of tourists in Hong Kong, the firm’s chairman said at the hotel’s opening ceremony on Tuesday. “The group established its first hotel, the Royal Garden Hotel, in Tsim Sha Tsui in 1981,” said Raymond Kwok Ping-luen, chairman and managing director of SHKP. “Subsequently, it opened many hotels in Hong Kong and mainland China because the group is very optimistic about the future of Hong Kong.” Kwok pointed out that Tseung Kwan O had developed rapidly over the past decade, and the community had undergone a complete transformation. “Therefore, this hotel renovation cannot simply replicate the old successful model, because the needs of guests have changed with time,” he said. The company had conducted in-depth research and analysis ahead of the renovation to gauge the needs of its customers, according to Kwok, as it strove “to provide the market with products and services that exceed their expectations”. The hotel could form a diverse and integrated lifestyle ecosystem with the group’s shopping malls, office buildings and residences located at Tseung Kwan O Station, Kwok added. Originally known as the Crowne Plaza Hong Kong Kowloon East, the hotel first opened in 2012 – becoming the first grade A luxury hotel in Tseung Kwan O at the time. While SHKP was the hotel’s owner and developer, the firm initially entrusted the management of the hotel to global hospitality firm InterContinental Hotels Group (IHG), which operated the facility under its Crowne Plaza brand. When the agreement between the two firms expired in late 2025, SHKP chose not to renew the contract and instead took back control of the facility in January. The developer decided to incorporate the facility into its own hotel brand, The Royal Garden, as part of an effort to bring it into line with changes in Hong Kong’s travel and tourism market. The rebranding involved a three-stage renovation project costing more than HK$100 million (US$12.75 million), which began midway through last year. The works increased the number of guest rooms by seven to 366.

title: Doctors warn of physical limits as China viral ‘flash step’ dance sends imitators to hospital
description: Veteran teacher says viral move appeals to the masses because it is both fun and witty – blending humour with professional skill.
content: A dance move known as the “flash step” recently went viral on Chinese social media, inspiring countless imitations, memes and creative merchandise, including keychains. In September, Chinese netizens jumped on the bandwagon, copying moves from a dance tutorial video made in the 1990s. They were especially taken with three moves featured in the video: the “flash step”, “prodigal kicking the ball” and “black bear shaking fur”. As its name vividly suggests, the flash step is a rapid, side-to-side dodging movement. “Prodigal kicking the ball” involves a rather bendy hopping kick with the arms outstretched, while “black bear shaking fur” features the dancer shaking vigorously, literally like a bear shaking its fur. Young people found the moves humorous and began imitating them and turning them into memes. The trend also caught the attention of celebrities, including Chinese idol and singer Lay Zhang Yixing, actress Li Yitong and even German fitness influencer Pamela Reif. These moves are actually from a professional folk dance tutorial film made by the Beijing Dance Academy. The two teachers who demonstrate them are Zhao Tiechun and Ming Wenjun, both veteran teachers at the academy. Furthermore, Ming is a former director-general of the Department of Art at the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, while Zhao was vice-president of the National Centre for the Performing Arts. The flash step and “prodigal kicking the ball”, performed by Zhao, are moves from the Flower Drum Lantern dance, a national-level intangible cultural heritage from central China’s Anhui province. The “black bear shaking fur” move comes from the drum-beating yangge folk dance of eastern China’s Shandong province. According to Professor Tian Lu of the academy’s Department of Chinese Ethnic and Folk Dance, who took part in filming, the moves’ vivid names are exactly the names used for them in those folk dances. For teaching purposes, the moves were extracted from the continuous sequences performed by folk dancers to train undergraduate students to shift their centre of gravity quickly and tilt their bodies into a pose. Tian told Chinese media outlet The Paper that the moves reflect the inherent humour of folk culture, expressed through these spontaneous dance movements. She also admitted that she had never imagined they would become so popular. However, teacher Zhao told Xinhua News Agency that he was not surprised. “The move has qualities that appeal to the masses. People find it fun and witty – both humorous and professional. The public’s collective creativity has generated this interesting phenomenon,” he said. After the moves went viral, Zhao also filmed himself leading a group of people in performing the flash step. The tutorial video that went viral was posted in 2018 by a dance graduate, who said he uploaded it simply to preserve the footage and share it with his peers. The poster, surnamed Duan, said that when they practised the moves in class, their teachers were strict about their posture, and they did not find the moves funny at all. As the moves were reinterpreted in memes, some social media users joked that the flash step helped them dodge people trying to assign them unwanted tasks. One user said it helped her get onto a metro train during rush hour. On Chinese e-commerce platforms, figures of Zhao and Ming from the video have also been turned into keychains and tapes, selling for around 10 to 20 yuan (US$1–3) each. Meanwhile, doctors have warned people copying the dance to be careful, as the moves require strong core, glute and thigh muscles. Those without professional dance training risk tearing a ligament. In response to the viral dance craze, the Affiliated Hospital of Yangzhou University issued a public warning, saying that within just a few days, orthopaedics and sports medicine clinics in multiple regions had reported treating a significant number of young patients injured while attempting the trend.

title: Former Chongqing mayor Huang Qifan under investigation for corruption
description: Huang had survived a number of regional scandals, including the downfalls of two of his former superiors, Bo Xilai and Sun Zhengcai.
content: Huang Qifan, former mayor of Chongqing and a survivor of multiple regional graft scandals, is under investigation for corruption, according to state media. State news agency Xinhua reported on Tuesday that the Communist Party’s Central Commission for Discipline Inspection was investigating Huang for alleged serious violations of discipline and law, a euphemism for corruption. Huang, 74, was mayor of the southwestern municipality from 2010 to 2016, overseeing an economic boom while navigating political scandals that brought down two of his former superiors, Bo Xilai and Sun Zhengcai. Bo, toppled in 2012, and Sun, brought down in 2017, were both Politburo members at the time they came under a corruption cloud. Beyond his political survival skills, Huang earned a reputation as a capable economic technocrat, nicknamed the “financial mayor” for his command of economic statistics and financial policy. Huang was also among the few provincial-level leaders who commented frequently on decisions made by the country’s financial regulators. He remained a prominent public commentator after leaving senior office, frequently delivering speeches on China’s economy, property market and financial reforms. In 2022, Huang warned that China’s property market had reached a turning point, questioning whether the country could sustain its decades-long construction boom. He was originally scheduled to attend two lectures this month. Huang was widely regarded as a long-term political survivor, having worked with six Chongqing party secretaries during his 15 years in the city. He retained his position after Bo, once considered a rising political star, was disgraced. Huang was credited as an architect of the economic growth associated with the “Chongqing model”, which emphasised state control over land and development projects. But under Bo’s leadership, the political aspects of the model – which heavily promoted revolutionary songs from the Mao Zedong era and nostalgia for Mao – soon raised alarm among the central leadership. At the same time, the municipality’s crackdown on crime resulted in numerous miscarriages of justice. Huang had previously enjoyed a close working relationship with Bo, describing their partnership as being “like fish and water” during an interview in 2010. After Bo’s downfall, however, Huang distanced himself from his former boss, criticising some of his projects as wasteful and pledging support for the central leadership’s decision to remove him. He testified in writing against his former superior, saying Bo’s decision to remove his police chief Wang Lijun had not been approved by the Ministry of Public Security. In another widely reported exchange during the annual legislative session in 2014, Huang was asked whether his relationship with Bo’s successor, Sun, was equally harmonious. He reportedly smiled without answering the question, prompting laughter from reporters. Sun was removed from his position in July 2017 and later sentenced to life imprisonment for bribery, but Huang, who had already stepped down as mayor, emerged from the second political storm without facing an investigation. However, some officials with close ties to Bo were investigated years after his downfall, including Xu Ming, the former party secretary of Chongqing’s Liangjiang New Area. Xu had worked with Bo at the Ministry of Commerce before following him to Chongqing in 2008. After Bo came under investigation, Xu was transferred to the post of deputy director of the State Administration of Grain. He retired in 2018 but came under investigation in 2021. He was credited with helping transform Chongqing from a traditional industrial centre into a major electronics manufacturing hub, attracting global technology companies and developing a vast laptop production industry. The municipality recorded economic growth of 11 per cent in 2015, among the fastest in China. After leaving Chongqing in December 2016, Huang was appointed vice-chairman of the National People’s Congress’ Financial and Economic Affairs Committee in February 2017. His tenure ended in 2018, when he retired. Born in Zhejiang province in 1952, Huang began his career as a factory worker in Shanghai before entering government service in the 1980s. He later held several senior positions and was closely involved in the development of Pudong, Shanghai’s financial and commercial district, paving the way for his transfer to Chongqing as vice-mayor in 2001.

title: Is Indonesia’s haze rhetoric ‘unempathetic’? Oxygen quip tests regional cooperation
description: Observers say Jakarta should acknowledge its shortcomings and welcome assistance to extinguish the fires.
content: An Indonesian official’s claim that the country exports “oxygen” and not just smoke to its neighbours has renewed criticism of Jakarta’s handling of its annual forest fires, with analysts warning that defensive nationalism risks undermining regional cooperation to tackle the recurring haze crisis. The remarks by Syahganda Nainggolan, the newly appointed head of the Government Communication Agency, reignited criticism over Indonesia’s handling of its ongoing forest and peatland fires, which have sent thick haze to Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei and parts of the Philippines. “We ask all our neighbours to understand that this is beyond human error, this is truly [caused by] nature,” Syahganda said on Saturday, as quoted by local news outlet Kompas. “We’re not just sending smoke. If there’s no smoke, we’re sending oxygen. Singapore and Malaysia’s oxygen comes from our forests.” This year’s fires have been exacerbated by slash-and-burn practices to clear land for plantations, alongside extreme drought attributed to a super El Nino. As of September 29, Indonesian police had arrested 196 suspects in connection with forest and land fires across the country. Syahganda’s comments, which triggered sarcasm and disbelief among social media users in Malaysia and Singapore, echoed a similarly controversial statement made by then vice-president Jusuf Kalla during the 2015 haze crisis when he claimed Indonesia sent “clean air” to Singapore and Malaysia for 11 months of the year “without being thanked”. ‘Concerning’ rhetoric The government’s dismissive narrative has also drawn criticism from foreign policy analysts, who argue that Jakarta should acknowledge its shortcomings and welcome assistance to extinguish the fires. “In my opinion, this statement reflects poorly on Indonesian diplomacy. It’s not only defensive, but also unempathetic and lacking in international etiquette,” said Shofwan Al Banna Choiruzzad, an associate professor of international relations at the University of Indonesia. He also warned that it would negatively affect Prabowo Subianto’s reputation and make Indonesia’s president a “common enemy” of its neighbours. Melinda Martinus, a fellow at the ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute’s Asean Studies Centre in Singapore, said the communications chief’s comments were “concerning because they risk framing a recurring environmental and public-health crisis as a natural phenomenon rather than a problem that also involves governance, land management and accountability”. “The concern is that such rhetoric can undermine the diplomatic goodwill needed to manage a transboundary crisis” and make it more difficult to advocate for regional cooperation through institutions such as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, Martinus added. Dafri Agussalim, a professor of international relations at Gadjah Mada University, called Syahganda’s remarks “inappropriate” and a form of “narrow nationalism”. Dafri urged Jakarta to “sit together” with its neighbours affected by the haze to coordinate responses and assistance, under the 2002 Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution framework. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim called Prabowo last week to voice his concern over the fires and offer help. “The haze situation is indeed worrying. I have personally contacted President Prabowo and he agreed to take the necessary steps,” Anwar said on Thursday. Malaysia’s foreign and environment ministers had contacted their Indonesian counterparts to “coordinate efforts to tackle forest and land fires and the resulting haze”, Anwar said, adding the he had also instructed his foreign minister Mohamad Hasan to engage Asean environment chiefs. However, Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi told the New Straits Times on Sunday that “there has been no response so far” to Malaysia’s outreach from Indonesia. “We are taking a positive view,” he said. “Perhaps they do not require our assistance.” Indonesia’s foreign minister Arrmanatha Nasir said on Saturday he had explained to Hasan the country’s firefighting efforts, such as “deploying more than 60,000 personnel and 48 helicopters and aircraft for water bombing and weather modification”. Shared responsibility On Monday, Prabowo ordered the deployment of 70,000 forest rangers to combat forest and peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan, which he said was “a top government priority”. Prabowo also called for stronger grass-roots measures to prevent similar cases from recurring. “We must step in to combat and prevent the fire in the most massive way possible,” he said during a cabinet meeting on Monday. As of Monday, fires had affected 129,899 hectares (320,987 acres) of peatland, of which 129,260 hectares had been extinguished, data from the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) showed. The firefighting measures are focused on six provinces, namely Riau, South Sumatra, Jambi, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan. BNPB head Suharyanto said on Monday that the fires in Central and South Kalimantan provinces were in “remote areas”, making it difficult for the task force to reach affected locations. Shofwan, the international-relations professor, also urged Indonesia to work with Singapore and Malaysia to jointly take action against plantation companies and financial firms involved in concessions where the fires occurred. Recent findings by environmental groups Greenpeace Indonesia, Greenpeace Malaysia and Pantau Gambut showed that among the 20 concessions emitting the most haze, “at least four” were linked to business groups based in Singapore, while one was tied to a Malaysian plantation group. Martinus said the 2002 Asean agreement on haze provided a regional framework for prevention, monitoring and cooperation, but not the enforcement authority to compel companies to pay compensation. “Asean can strengthen cooperation on documenting evidence and enforcement,” she said. “This could involve more systematic sharing of hotspot data, concession maps, corporate ownership information and investigation findings, subject to applicable laws and evidentiary requirements.”

title: China’s Zhuhai air show to feature first dedicated naval equipment display
description: New exhibition area marks another expansion of country’s largest air show, as the PLA doubles down on developing its naval capabilities.
content: In a first, China’s biggest air show will feature a dedicated naval equipment exhibition area, showcasing hardware in service with the country’s navy, according to the event’s organisers. This year is the 30th anniversary of the biennial China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, also known as the Zhuhai air show, which displays China’s civilian and military aircraft for international buyers. A number of China’s aircraft have debuted at the event, including the J-20 stealth fighter, which made its first public flight during the 2016 edition. Co-hosted by the Guangdong provincial government and the PLA Air Force, the event is organised by the Zhuhai municipal government. This year’s edition is set to take place in the southern coastal city from December 7 to 13, one day longer than the previous edition, according to the organisers. “For the first time, this year’s air show will expand into the maritime domain, with a naval equipment exhibition area at Gaolan Port, allowing a large-scale display of equipment currently in service with the navy,” Zhang Hu, vice-governor of Guangdong province, said in Beijing on Tuesday. Zhang said this year’s exhibition would be the biggest yet, with the indoor display area expanding by a further 12.5 per cent. More than 3,000 pieces of equipment will be on show and about 10 per cent of the exhibits will be making their debut. The naval equipment exhibition area marks another expansion of the Zhuhai air show as China doubles down on developing its naval capabilities. The organisers said the Chinese navy would use nearly 1km (0.62 miles) of shoreline at Gaolan Port for the exhibition, with active-duty warships on static display and equipment such as amphibious armoured vehicles showcased on land. The PLA Southern Theatre Command, which oversees Chinese military operations across the South China Sea, is among the supporting organisations for this year’s edition. Zhang said the dedicated drone exhibition area would feature counter-drone demonstrations involving several new types of anti-drone systems. Major General Gao Xiang, deputy director of the PLA Air Force’s political work department, said: “Several types of major combat equipment will make their debut … with systematic displays of the air force’s reconnaissance, early warning, air defence, support, uncrewed applications, intelligent equipment and munitions.” Gao said the exhibition would feature both mature combat equipment that had been put to the test and the public unveiling of several upgraded systems and new combat capabilities. In addition, the air force would showcase its latest achievements in intelligent coordination involving uncrewed systems, he added. Gao did not say which specific models of equipment would be exhibited. Hao Changfeng, a spokesman for Chinese aerospace giant China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation, said the group would stage its largest-ever display of heavy-lift launch vehicles and reusable rockets at the air show. The exhibition will also feature dedicated sections for companies from France, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Brazil and the United States, with Airbus, Boeing and Embraer among the exhibitors. The PLA Air Force’s August 1st aerobatic team, the Russian Aerospace Forces’ Russian Knights and the United Arab Emirates’ Al Fursan aerobatic team are set to perform at the event.

title: Meet Trump’s new press secretary Katie Zacharia’s husband, Tyler – who’s a film producer
description: The former Fox News commentator replaces Karoline Leavitt – what do we know about her husband, who worked on projects like Martin Scorsese’s Silence?
content: US President Donald Trump said he has appointed conservative commentator and Truth Social communications adviser Katie Zacharia as his new press secretary. “She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning. She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of Maga!” Trump posted on social media. “I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the media, the American people, and my administration.” Zacharia replaces Karoline Leavitt, who had served as the president’s chief spokesperson during his second term until she departed at the end of August, saying that she wanted to spend more time with family. In his announcement, the president also cited Zacharia’s stint as a spokesperson at the Department of Homeland Security and her role as a commentator on Fox News and Newsmax. “Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honour of a lifetime,” Zacharia said in a post on X. As Zacharia assumes her new role ahead of the looming midterm elections, here’s everything you need to know about her husband, Tyler Zacharia. What is Tyler Zacharia’s background? Tyler Zacharia is an entertainment and investment executive who has produced several films, including Martin Scorsese’s Silence (2016), The Irishman (2019) and Countdown (2019). Tyler started his career in 2005 as a research analyst at the National Bureau of Asian Research. According to his LinkedIn profile, he spent eight years in Beijing working in private equity before moving on to various media investment companies. He currently serves as the chief operating officer at 2521 Entertainment, where he leads operations, finance and deal-making. Katie and Tyler Zacharia have 4 kids While it’s unclear how Katie and Tyler met, both worked in Beijing around the same time. According to their LinkedIn profiles, Katie was in Beijing from 2011 to 2013, while her husband worked there from 2007 to 2013. The couple reportedly tied the knot in 2011 and have since welcomed four children, whom they are raising in Southern California, per Newsweek. On September 18, Katie took to Instagram to share a family photo, blurring out her children’s faces, and wrote in the caption: “Being in the world of politics, whether directly or adjacent, is brutal ... and I personally take daily heat for it. I try to keep my family away from the flame. However, this year I’m particularly proud of my husband, who made David, Brink of War, Young Washington and many other great movies for @angel.” “Different lanes, but God, country, family, and as our kids know, in CA, we proudly support President Trump,” she continued. With additional reporting by Bloomberg

title: Drones hit 2 ships off Bulgaria, sinking 1 and triggering Black Sea search for 11
description: Eleven sailors are missing after drone strikes sank a cargo ship off Bulgaria, as Sofia summons Russia’s envoy and seeks Nato help.
content: Drones struck two ships in the Black Sea off Bulgaria on Tuesday, sinking one and prompting emergency rescue operations, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. The Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Dignity sank after it was hit by a military strike. Five sailors were rescued, while a search for the other 11 crew members continued, Varna district governor Mario Smrkov said. Rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members from one ship, the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries, Radev said in a video posted to social media. The crew, which included seven Ukrainian citizens and eight Azerbaijani citizens, reported the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones. The strikes on the two ships occurred 20 miles (32km) and 21 miles (34km) from the Bulgarian coast. During an emergency meeting of Bulgaria’s Security Council on Tuesday, Radev called the attacks “absolutely unacceptable” and said Bulgaria was seeking Nato and European Union help. While authorities did not possess clear evidence on who was responsible for the drone attacks, “it makes no sense for Ukraine to destroy its own ships in the Black Sea, and the results of these strikes favour Russia’s interests”, Radev told the Russian ambassador in Sofia during a meeting on Tuesday, the government’s press office reported. The ambassador said that she did not have any information from the Russian defence ministry related to the recent attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea but added that she did not rule out the possibility that “these attacks represent a provocation by a third party”. Radev has said that such attacks were unacceptable and that Bulgaria would continue to investigate the attacks together with its EU and Nato allies to establish the truth. Radev said that Bulgaria was suffering significant economic and financial damage and added that his country would initiate talks with neighbouring Romania and Turkey on joint proposals to guarantee the safety of shipping in the Black Sea. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha in a post on social media on Tuesday blamed Russia for the attacks. “Russia’s latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria’s territorial waters, which injured Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens, once again demonstrates Moscow’s deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea,” Sybiha wrote. He said that Ukraine was urging its partners to step up pressure on Russia, strengthen sanctions and take decisive action to hold it accountable and protect freedom of navigation. “The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage. This must be met with strength,” Sybiha wrote. “Nato will continue to work closely with our Allies in the Black Sea,” Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte wrote on social media. He added that Nato had already strengthened its posture along the eastern flank and would continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting its deterrence and defence posture as needed. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen “strongly condemned” the drone incidents and said the Black Sea “has become another front of escalation” in Russia’s war in Ukraine. “This is unacceptable. I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast. Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea,” she said in a post on social media. “We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response. Those responsible should be held accountable.” European Council President Antonio Costa said in a social media post that the EU stood in full solidarity with Bulgaria following the attacks. Costa said the growing number of Russian hybrid activities would be discussed at the European Council meeting scheduled for Thursday and Friday in Brussels. The attacks came exactly a week after sea and aerial drones attacked two other commercial vessels in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea. A Togo-flagged ship sank, while a Bulgarian ferry evacuated the 18-member crew of a Pulau-flagged vessel. A day earlier, a Turkish-owned cargo ship carrying corn caught fire following a drone attack and later sank in the Black Sea off the coast of Romania. Two people died and 11 crew members were rescued, Romanian authorities said.

title: Rarely seen US$180 million Van Gogh on show in Hong Kong ahead of New York auction
description: The US$450 million Blaquier-Arrieta Collection, including Van Gogh’s Chataigniers en fleurs, is currently on view at Sotheby’s Hong Kong.
content: A collection of Impressionist and post-Impressionist masterpieces – including a rarely seen landscape painting by Vincent van Gogh – which have been hidden from public view for more than half a century, will be going under the hammer this November. The Blaquier-Arrieta Collection has made its global debut in Hong Kong, with a dozen works on show until October 15, before being put up for auction at Sotheby’s in New York. The collection, amassed by the Argentinian businessman Carlos Pedro Blaquier and art patron Maria Elena “Nelly” Arrieta de Blaquier – both deceased – has an estimated value of US$450 million (HK$3.53 billion). This collection is the likes of which just cannot be assembled today Scott Niichel of Sotheby’s It traces the rise of modern art, from the birth of Impressionism in the early 1870s through to the dawn of fauvism in the early 20th century. “This collection is the likes of which just cannot be assembled today,” says Scott Niichel, vice-chairman and head of middle market for Modern & Contemporary Art at Sotheby’s. “Collected mostly in the 1970s, these works are truly all the best in class and acquired from some of the finest dealers and collections in the world.” The centrepiece of the collection is Van Gogh’s Chataigniers en fleurs (Chestnut Trees in Flower), painted in May 1890, just over two months before the Dutch artist’s death. The work is expected to fetch US$180 million, beating the existing auction record for the artist. Having spent a year at an asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France, recovering from a mental health crisis and the mutilation of his ear, Van Gogh came to Auvers-Sur-Oise near Paris on the recommendation of his friend Dr Paul Gachet, who lived in the village. The move represented a fresh start. Van Gogh threw himself into work there with remarkable energy during a period that Niichel describes as “a moment of tremendous creativity and hopefulness”. It was a time when the artist painted gardens, wheat fields and the chestnut trees that lined the streets near his lodgings – trees he would have passed daily and likely come to know intimately. The work is one of only eight of the 50 landscape paintings Van Gogh produced in Auvers that remain in private hands, and was one of the last great works by the artist to appear on the public market. The second headline work is Paul Cezanne’s Arlequin – or Harlequin – a portrait of the artist’s son Paul dressed in the costume of the commedia dell’arte character. Estimated to sell for US$120 million, it is one of four images the French post-Impressionist painter created between 1888 and 1890 of his son in this guise. Niichel notes that the first painting in the series is at the Pushkin Museum in Moscow, Russia, the second at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, in the US, and a third, smaller version at the Pola Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan. “This is the only remaining work in private hands,” Niichel says. “It’s also one of very few figure paintings by the artist that remain in private hands.” The portrait holds a deeply personal significance. Cezanne kept his relationship with his wife Marie-Hortense and their son Paul largely hidden for years, fearing the loss of his inheritance from his father. The series was created shortly after his father’s death. “The fact that he’s representing his son here as this trickster in this flamboyant costume really speaks to this pride and this kind of more rebellious story,” Niichel says. The scope of the entire collection being sold extends well beyond these two works. Among the highlights is one of Camille Pissarro’s Avenue de l’Opera paintings – La Place du Theatre-Français et l’avenue de l’Opera, soleil d’apres-midi en hiver (1898) – one of the finest examples of the artist’s depictions of Parisian boulevards, estimated to sell in excess of US$30 million, as well as Pierre-Auguste Renoir’s En Canot (Jeune fille a la barque), a portrait of the artist’s muse Marguerite, painted in 1877. Paintings by Claude Monet, Paul Gauguin and Alfred Sisley are also part of the showcase. The works will be on view in Hong Kong until October 15 at Sotheby’s Maison, Landmark Chater, Central, before travelling to Paris and then New York, where the dedicated auction will take place on November 18. For more information, visit sothebys.com.

title: China’s Guangdong province sets ambitious targets for advanced manufacturing by 2028
description: Officials want to increase adoption of AI in factories, boost production of humanoid robots.
content: China’s most populous province has set ambitious targets for advanced manufacturing by 2028, including the production of more than 80,000 humanoid robots a year, to strengthen its position as a global industrial powerhouse despite concerns about domestic demand and export barriers. Guangdong, which boasts a population of 129 million people and one of the oldest factory bases in the country, aims to build over 1,000 top-performing smart factories in the next two years as well as 1,000 green factories, the People’s Daily website reported on Tuesday, citing information given by officials at an advanced manufacturing conference on Friday. Green factories would be assessed for energy efficiency, resource use and environmental performance, conference participants said. Guangdong officials also said they want the AI adoption rate among manufacturers with annual main business revenue of 20 million yuan (US$2.98 million) or higher to exceed 50 per cent within two years. Shu Yang, product and presales technology director at industrial robot maker KUKA China, told the conference the company’s Shunde base had raised its core component localisation rate above 90 per cent, Nanfang Daily reported. “Models produced at German factories can now also be made in China, while some models made in China cannot necessarily be produced in Germany,” he was quoted as saying. Major manufacturers in Guangdong, which has 10 industrial clusters each worth more than 1 trillion yuan, generated 19.34 trillion yuan in revenue last year, the highest among China’s provinces, People’s Daily reported, citing official provincial data. At an “AI plus” manufacturing event hosted by Guangdong’s Department of Industry and Information Technology last month, the province disclosed that over 2,000 embodied-intelligence robots had entered industrial use this year for sorting, loading, handling, inspection and collaborative tasks. Except for exports, which remain a rare bright spot, both fixed-asset investment and consumption remain sluggish Peng Peng, Guangdong Society of Reform Peng Peng, executive chairman of the Guangdong Society of Reform, a think tank associated with the provincial government, said the 2028 targets reflected a strategic shift towards building “world-class and globally competitive” factory hubs and integrating artificial intelligence applications. The province was doubling down on those goals to shore up an economic growth rate that trailed the national average, he said. “Except for exports, which remain a rare bright spot, both fixed-asset investment and consumption remain sluggish,” Peng said. However, apart from the property sector, investment “looks decent, driven by strong growth in advanced manufacturing and hi-tech sectors”, he said. AI offered a “promising” way to combine Guangdong’s manufacturing base with technological innovation, Peng added. Guangdong’s rise to become a manufacturing hub began in the late 1970s, coinciding with the introduction of China’s “reform and opening-up” policy under former leader Deng Xiaoping. David Wong, a lecturer at Hang Seng University of Hong Kong, said it was unclear whether domestic and overseas markets could absorb the additional factory output envisioned by 2028. Heavy factory automation could displace workers, resulting in lower wages and fewer jobs that would impose further constraints on household spending, Wong said. Exports from Guangdong’s factories face uncertainty as the United States and the European Union scrutinise Chinese hi-tech products and pursue trade negotiations, he added. China and the EU reached a trade deal this month that would impose strict quotas on Chinese hybrid car exports to Europe.

title: Houthi official warns US against entering war in Yemen as Saudis weather attacks
description: Rebel group threatens US interests while aviation notice shows Riyadh airport operations suspended through October 17.
content: A Houthi official has warned the US it would receive a “painful response” if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington’s help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks. Yemen’s civil war - in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis - reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis. The Houthis quickly began targeting Saudi oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs, including a string of lethal strikes on Riyadh’s airport, rocking the world’s top oil exporter. Blasts resounded over the capital again on Monday night, with the Saudi coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile and the group saying it had again targeted the airport. Later, the coalition announced that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles in the south of the kingdom, near the border with Yemen. In a statement posted on social media, the coalition said it had “intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Khamis Mushait”, a city where a Saudi military base has previously come under attacks. Following an attack at the Riyadh airport on Saturday that killed 13 people, US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom. “The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. They’re misbehaving very badly. No good,” Trump said on Monday. “If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti said in an interview. He also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”. Saturday’s strike on King Khalid International Airport was the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, and also left hundreds wounded. Trump said the attack was “not acceptable” and that he would be speaking to the kingdom’s de facto leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, telling reporters the US was “going to look at” the possibility of joining Saudi strikes. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh’s outskirts on Monday, with a notice to airmen (NOTAM) showing it would remain closed until 2100 GMT on October 17. Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”. Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told a conference in Riyadh on Monday that the recent events had “tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people and our resilience”. “The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.” Tensions escalated further on Tuesday evening as a Saudi-led coalition spokesperson said a warning would be issued shortly for civilians to evacuate a site in Yemen’s capital of Sanaa ahead of a special operation. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree warned that any strikes on Sanaa would be met with a “harsh and painful” response in the Saudi capital Riyadh. CCTV footage of Saturday’s attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden blast tore through the building and brought down flaming debris. The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats. In the evening, mobile phones received a loud government alert warning of a “hostile aerial threat” before the announcement of the interception. The alert delayed the kickoff of a football match between Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana and Saudi team Al Nassr, home to Portuguese superstar Cristiano Ronaldo. It was the first use of the phone alert system in Riyadh in weeks, with no official reason given for the lack of messaging during the attacks targeting the capital in recent days. The Houthis said they had also targeted the Khamis Mushait base in the kingdom’s south with a drone. The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said US government employees must obtain its authorisation before using any airport in the kingdom, and urged US citizens to “take extreme caution” if they chose to do so. The mission also said “American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events” in Saudi Arabia. The UAE’s national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week, and also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah. Bahrain’s national carrier Gulf Air said it too was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday. US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh, scheduled for October 23. Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences. Riyadh leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa. The long-running Yemeni civil war has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country. UN rights chief Volker Turk said he was “appalled by the repeated attacks” on Saudi Arabia, but urged both sides to back down, adding “continued fighting will only unleash further misery with no end in sight”. Additional reporting by Reuters

title: British Council to resume IELTS exams after 4-day stoppage across China
description: Organisation cites technical problems for disruptions that hit at the height of overseas university admissions season for mainland students.
content: IELTS examinations will resume across China on Wednesday, the British Council said after four days of cancellations that left test-takers scrambling at the height of the overseas university admissions season. The organisation announced on Tuesday afternoon that it would hold two free make-up sessions – on October 19 and 20 – for affected candidates and reimburse reasonable travel and accommodation costs for those who travelled to testing centres. The cancellations, which began on Saturday and continued through to Tuesday, marked a rare nationwide breakdown since the International English Language Testing System was introduced to mainland China in 1989. Without elaborating, the British Council attributed the suspensions to “technical problems” and classified the disruptions as force majeure, according to Chinese media. In a statement on its Chinese website on Tuesday, the organisation said the technical failure “may have affected examination security” and that cancelling the affected sessions had been necessary “to safeguard the fairness, impartiality and credibility of the test”. It also announced several remedial measures. Affected test-takers will receive a full refund, and those who have already registered for other dates can retain their existing bookings while receiving either a refund for one test fee or a transfer to a make-up session free of charge. Candidates who cannot attend the October make-up dates and have not yet registered for another sitting will receive a free voucher for the same test type, valid until the end of December. The disruptions occurred just weeks after traditional paper-based IELTS examinations in mainland China ended in September, with computer-delivered testing now the only method. It is not clear how many people have been affected by the cancellations. National Business Daily reported that a staff member from China’s National Education Examinations Authority – which partners with the British Council to administer the exams – said the organisation had decided unilaterally to cancel the tests. IELTS examinations are not offered in all Chinese cities so many candidates must travel to other areas and arrange transport and accommodation. The disruptions hit at a critical time for mainland Chinese students applying to universities in Hong Kong, Britain, Singapore and other destinations, with the autumn application season typically between September and October. Some candidates hold conditional offers that require verified language results to secure their places. The cancellation included IELTS One Skill Retake, an option enabling test-takers who previously completed all four sections to repeat only a single component – listening, reading, writing or speaking – to boost their overall results. On Chinese social media platforms, distressed candidates shared accounts of sudden operational paralysis and dashed timelines. A number of affected test-takers reported that automated cancellation notices arrived as late as 9pm on the evening before their scheduled sitting. Many candidates had already paid for hotels and travel arrangements. Some also complained that they might not be able to meet application deadlines for institutions next week. Meanwhile, test centres operated independently by IDP IELTS Australia have operated uninterrupted. On Sunday, the Melbourne-based company, which manages 29 computer-delivered centres in mainland China, announced it would open extra IELTS exam slots between October 17 and October 31 to help affected candidates.

title: China’s Iluvatar CoreX’s first AI computing supernode squeezes most GPUs in 1 system
description: The new system reduces token costs by 40 per cent, offering a local alternative amid US curbs.
content: Chinese AI chipmaker Iluvatar CoreX debuted its first supernode system, a computing system that squeezes 144 graphics processing units (GPUs) into a single cabinet, breaking an industrial record. The new product, dubbed the Tiangai 300 IXL144, was unveiled on Monday at the 2026 China International Industry Fair (CIIF) in Shanghai. Designed for large-scale AI model training and inference, the system packs 144 GPUs and 18 central processing units (CPUs) into a single cabinet and boasts around 10.1 terabytes of memory, according to the company. Supernodes deeply integrate computation, storage, networking, management and software frameworks into a single supercomputer. As US export controls continue to restrict access to advanced chips from Nvidia alongside surging AI demand, the proliferation of interconnected cabinet systems is increasingly seen as a resource to scale computing power. Iluvatar said that the system had a flexible single-cabinet architecture and that its efforts in improving efficiency could lower the cost per 1 million valid tokens by 40 per cent compared with “mainstream international alternatives”. The move by Iluvatar reflects how Chinese chip companies – from tech giants like Huawei Technologies to pure-play AI chipmakers – are rushing to unveil supernode products that host self-developed chips. Iluvatar is a relative latecomer in the domestic market as its supernode systems come months after those of its peers, MetaX and Enflame, amid the intense pressure to establish market share. “A supernode isn’t a single product, but a systems engineering project where the ultimate competition is over economic efficiency,” said Zou Xuan, vice-president of Iluvatar. The company said its Tiangai chip series had already achieved 10,000-card scale deployments, which equipped the company with crucial experience in system-level delivery and operations maintenance. Supernode products are part of Iluvatar’s broader efforts to promote its product mix upgrade towards next-generation AI computing boards, which “carry stronger computing power and higher average selling prices”, according to a recent research note by Goldman Sachs. The CIIF exhibition floor also featured products from MetaX and Enflame – two rivals of Iluvatar. At the event, which runs from Monday to Friday, MetaX displayed its Xijing S600 supernode, which packs 64 fully interconnected GPUs into a cabinet and is able to scale up to 10,000-card clusters. Enflame, backed by Tencent Holdings, showcased its CloudBlazer ESL64-O, a high-performance supernode system using an orthogonal hardware architecture, which it co-developed with telecommunications equipment company ZTE. Both products were unveiled in July. Iluvatar, which went public in Hong Kong earlier this year, swung to profitability for the first time in the first half of 2026, posting a net profit of 106 million yuan (US$15.83 million). Revenue surged over 191 per cent to 945.7 million yuan, with its core general-purpose GPU products generating 916.1 million yuan.

title: Japan, US review military liberty policies after Okinawa killing
description: Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi says high-level talks will target off-base curfew enforcement and joint patrols after a US marine’s arrest.
content: Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said on Tuesday that officials were reviewing the off-base code of conduct for US troops in Japan following the alleged killing of an Okinawan woman by a US marine. Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-runs and drunk driving by US military personnel have long triggered protests on the southern Japanese island, which has for years urged other regions in the country to share the burden of hosting US troops. “We plan to hold discussions including whether the existing rules are effectively functioning,” Motegi said, adding that “matters such as patrols and curfew management” would be under review in talks with the United States. The high-level bilateral consultations would examine off-duty conduct and the “liberty” policy governing off-base private activities of US military personnel, he said. The existing policy, updated in 2024 following a string of sexual assaults by US military personnel in Okinawa, includes a ban on US military personnel drinking in public off base between 1am and 5am or going to bars during those hours. Japanese police arrested a US marine stationed on Okinawa last week on suspicion of killing a 39-year-old woman at a hotel in the capital Naha. The US military enacted a two-day operational pause after the marine’s arrest to reinforce discipline and standards, followed by a month-long curfew from midnight. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Tuesday that “we began high-level, working-level consultations between Japan and the United States last week on what effective measures should be taken”. “The Japanese government will continue to do everything in its power both to address this case and to ensure that it does not happen again,” she told a legislative committee session. Motegi held a telephone call at the weekend with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who offered his “sincere condolences” over the alleged crime, pledging US cooperation in the investigation. Crimes committed by US personnel have been a thorn in relations between the close security allies. Last year, a Japanese court sentenced a US marine accused of choking and attempting to rape a woman in her 20s to seven years in prison. The United States has around 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa.

title: Hongkong Post contract staff to be prioritised for other civil service roles
description: Civil Service Bureau offers relaxed academic requirements for clerical posts, but union head says measures may still fall short.
content: Hundreds of Hong Kong postal workers denied the chance to secure permanent contracts will be prioritised for alternative civil service positions and granted lower entry hurdles for clerical jobs as the mail authority wrestles with a record deficit. The Civil Service Bureau unveiled the concessions on Tuesday to support staff affected by Hongkong Post’s unprecedented cost-cutting measures. The government department announced in August it would stop offering permanent civil service positions to about 200 employees on probation, offering them two-year contracts instead. “The government understands the worries of the affected staff about their future career prospects, and that they may consider applying for other jobs, including other civil service positions. Therefore, the bureau has introduced special recruitment and appointment arrangements,” a bureau spokesman said in response to a South China Morning Post inquiry. “Hongkong Post will continue to maintain close communication with the affected staff and provide timely assistance, such as skills training.” The bureau said affected employees seeking other civil service jobs would bypass shortlisting straight into the first round of selection, and would be given priority over rival candidates in the event of a tie score. It would also launch a one-off special scheme allowing affected staff to transfer to assistant clerical officer or clerical assistant posts with relaxed academic qualifications, though candidates must still pass skills tests and interviews. Details will be announced in the first quarter of next year. The government guaranteed that affected workers would suffer no pay cuts if the starting salary of their new role was lower. Those who have already completed probation at Hongkong Post will bypass the standard three-year probationary period in their new roles, serving only a one-year trial period. Lawmaker Lam Wai-kong, who represents the labour sector and attended a briefing with the bureau, said the government was considering relaxing minimum academic qualifications for workers applying for assistant clerical officer or clerical assistant posts from passing five subjects in the Diploma of Secondary Education exam or the Hong Kong Certificate of Education Examination to just three: Chinese, English and mathematics. Lam noted that the special concession targeted these two grades because of existing manpower shortages and because recruitment was managed directly by the bureau, making support measures easier to implement. Affected staff would also be permitted to apply for internal transfers to other departments – a privilege usually restricted to permanent civil servants, Lam noted. Welcoming the measures, Lam said they provided more options for affected workers, noting that some had originally transferred to the postal service from other departments and could now return to their initial posts more easily. Tsoi Koon-lung, president of the Hong Kong Chinese Civil Servants’ Association, said workers applying for other civil service posts would still have to go through an open recruitment process, including skill tests and interviews, to guarantee fairness and ensure basic requirements were met. But he cautioned that the remedial measures might still fall short, reiterating that the best solution was to reverse the initial decision to deny permanent contracts – a problem he insisted had been created by the administration. “When they attend interviews, they might be at a disadvantage because they did not originally intend to take up clerical work,” Tsoi said. “Of course, their advantage is their experience working in government. So in the end, it depends on whether individual colleagues have sufficient competitiveness.” Hong Kong Postal Workers Union chairman Cheung Wai-kuen welcomed the relief package, saying it addressed the demands of affected employees. While acknowledging the difference between postal and clerical work, he noted Hongkong Post had provided training in typing and office software to give the workers the skills they would need to make the pivot. Cheung said staff who had recently joined the post office, as well as those who had completed probation, would have strong incentives to apply elsewhere, as a fresh trial period presented minimal disruption to their careers. The self-financing postal service has bled money for eight straight years, reporting a record deficit of HK$821 million (US$105.3 million) in 2024-25. The Legislative Council previously approved a HK$4.6 billion bailout to prop up operations over the next three years, while the government has pledged to unveil a reform road map by 2028.

title: Opinion | Trump-Xi summit threw up a hard question for Japan: national dignity
description: Tokyo needs to recalibrate what constitutes true national dignity with respect to its relationships with the US and China.
content: One day before Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Washington for his summit with Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi secured her own audience with the US president – which was followed by a phone call after Xi departed. Her preoccupation was ensuring that Tokyo’s interests were not quietly traded away in a US-China bargain. Beneath this diplomacy lies a question Japan has not yet answered for itself: whether Takaichi’s response to perceived security challenges reflects a broad-based grass-roots consensus or her revival of an older, inherited idea of national identity that has never been fully reckoned with. While little substantial agreement was reached at the US-China summit, what Tokyo found most alarming was Trump recalling the history of how the US and China were allies in the fight against Japan during World War II. A few days earlier, in her United Nations speech, Takaichi had called for the removal of Japan’s wartime “enemy state” label from the UN Charter. During the Cold War, Japan was a key bulwark against communism in the Western Pacific: the Soviet Union, China and North Korea. But in the current world order, Japan needs America more than the US needs it. Tokyo must reckon with the contingency that Washington may pursue a great-power bargain with Beijing that diverges from Japan’s security priorities. Why did Takaichi choose a confrontational stance with China? Ideological conviction came first. Long before she held power, Takaichi believed that Japan must become a “normal” state, unconstrained by the pacifist limits its post-war constitution placed on defence. As an intellectual protege of former prime minister Shinzo Abe, she has for decades belonged to the ultraconservative Nippon Kaigi lobby group, whose platform treats military normalisation and the restoration of the emperor’s centrality to Japan’s national polity as two sides of the same historical revisionist project which rejects war guilt. That conviction might have remained a minority position, tempered by the Liberal Democratic Party’s internal factional balance as it had been for decades. But the forces that once restrained Japan’s hardliners weakened sharply in 2024. The landslide victory that followed early this year, delivering the LDP more than two-thirds of the lower house, converted what had been a factional minority view into a governing mandate. While Japan’s post-war generation achieved dignity and security through economic success, younger voters who grew up in the lost decades face greater economic precarity. As the traditional ladders of career progression and home ownership become less attainable, national prestige may be a more attractive status good. Takaichi’s tough stance is no fluke but a coherent position arising from these factors. Yet there is the unresolved tension of whether kokutai, the abstract national polity anchored to the emperor, or the people of Japan deserve the ultimate loyalty. While popular sovereignty may be enshrined in Japan’s post-war constitution, kokutai is resiliently alive behind different facades. Defeated by the US in the second world war, Tokyo has long accepted a subordinate position to Washington. But Japan was the leading economic and technological power in Asia for decades, and remains the only Asian member of the Group of 7. In Japan’s political tradition, national dignity has been about being accepted as a peer of the West and standing above other Asian countries. But that construct needs updating in a rising Asia as China has become the only peer of the US. Perhaps Japan needs to recalibrate what constitutes true national dignity with respect to its relationships with the US and China. While Japan has less than one-tenth the population of China, scale is hardly the defining criterion for dignity. Singapore is among the most respected countries in the world. With an ageing population, stagnant economy, high indebtedness and a weak yen, Japan faces a myriad of economic and social challenges. Even if it has the technological base, does Japan have the fiscal and human resources to remilitarise? Just as cheap imports from China and exports of critical components to China have sustained the quality of life in Japan over decades of economic stagnancy, the welfare of the Japanese people is based on friendly relationships with key Asian neighbours. The geopolitical predicament facing Japan is real but partly internal and self-imposed, stemming from a national identity issue unresolved since the Meiji Restoration. At the core is a question Japan has postponed since 1945: should the ultimate loyalty be owed to the people, or to a conception of the nation inherited from the emperor-centred past? The American occupation established a democratic form for Japan but left its deeper kokutai merely dormant – and it’s now being stirred back to life by Takaichi. Japan’s people deserve a national security architecture accountable to their genuine welfare, not one that treats them as instruments of an abstract national ideal. The real test facing the Japanese is this: 80 years on, will they finally claim the right to define their own dignity?

title: North Korea’s new missile museum: part shrine, part arms bazaar
description: Analysts say the museum was built to woo foreign buyers, burnish national pride and bury disarmament talks for good.
content: North Korea now has a museum for its bombs. The National Defence Revolution Museum, which opened on Sunday, is the country’s first dedicated exclusively to military hardware, from rifles to intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs). Observers say it is also intended to send a message to Washington and Seoul, serve as a permanent showroom for the North’s arms exports and visibly enshrine its nuclear programme as an irreversible part of state policy. Third-generation ruler Kim Jong-un cut the ribbon to open the museum, then toured the exhibits with his wife Ri Sol-ju and his daughter Kim Ju-ae by his side. He called the museum an “immortal” repository of the country’s arms development and one of its “national treasures”. Photographs in the ruling Workers’ Party newspaper, Rodong Sinmun, showed combat kit, drones and ballistic missiles, including the Hwasong-20 ICBM, an untested next-generation system North Korea claims will be capable of striking anywhere in the United States. Other exhibits include a submarine-launched ballistic missile, a Hwasong-16Ma hypersonic missile, a 600mm super-large multiple rocket launcher and the Bada-suri anti-ship missile. In front of the Hwasong-20 display stood diagrams of multiple-warhead technology and a world map illustrating missile strike ranges, from South America to Australia and the Middle East. In his speech at Sunday’s opening ceremony, Kim said the museum showcased how the “dignity and security” of the state were protected “and how peace on this land has been secured”, according to state media “The scale and content of the museum will be expanded and enriched day by day,” he added. Hawking hardware North Korea has been staging regular arms fairs since 2021 to showcase the modernisation of its military, including a weapons expo three years ago attended by Russia’s then defence minister. Against this backdrop, establishing a permanent museum was “a natural progression” for a leader who pursued projects “intended to burnish his record”, said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies. By gathering the weapons built under Kim’s rule, Lim said the regime aimed to show that its defence science programme had reached an advanced stage and to preserve the achievements as part of Kim’s legacy. Such “a permanent symbolic venue for showcasing the regime’s achievements and promoting its political narrative” also signalled “a strong determination to cement North Korea’s status as a nuclear-armed state … rather than treating its nuclear arsenal as a bargaining chip in future denuclearisation negotiations”, Lim said. Oh Gyeong-seob, a senior research fellow at the Korea Institute for National Unification, agreed that the museum would make it “all the more difficult to solve the nuclear issue through dialogue” in future. A permanent museum also suggested that Pyongyang wanted weapons displays to be a routine feature of public life, not something confined to periodic exhibitions and parades, said Yang Moo-jin, a professor at the University of North Korean Studies. It also appeared designed as a tourist attraction for domestic and foreign visitors, including potential arms buyers from Russia, Iran, Pakistan and the Middle East, Yang said. But he added a caveat. “The exhibits are believed to comprise a mixture of genuine weapons, replicas and empty shells,” Yang said. “Strategic weapons may have been displayed as empty shells to address safety and security concerns and prevent the leakage of sensitive technology.” Inheriting the bomb Domestically, the message was one of endurance.
